1	---
2	name: mlflow-tracking
3	description: Set up and operate MLflow for ML experiment tracking, model registry, and LLM tracing in any Python project. Covers three deployment modes — local file (`./mlruns`), local SQLite + `mlflow ui` (recommended for solo experiments), and a production Docker Compose stack with PostgreSQL + MinIO (vendored as a ready-to-copy `assets/docker-compose-stack/`). Use whenever the user wants to log params/metrics/artifacts, manage models with aliases (Champion/Challenger), enable framework autologging (sklearn/pytorch/lightning/xgboost/transformers/etc.), trace LLM calls (OpenAI/Anthropic/LangChain/LlamaIndex/DSPy), spin up a self-hosted tracking server, or asks about `mlflow.set_tracking_uri` / `mlflow.start_run` / `mlflow.<framework>.autolog` / `mlflow ui` / `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`. Always references the official docs at https://mlflow.org/docs/latest and the upstream repo https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow — MLflow ships fast, prefer fetching live docs over relying on memory.
4	---
5	
6	# MLflow Tracking
7	
8	MLflow gives you experiment tracking, a model registry, and (since 2.14+) first-class LLM observability — all from one Python library + UI. Unlike DVC it **does** require a tracking backend (file / SQLite / server), but it gives you a real dashboard and multi-user collaboration in return.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about the **three deployment modes that actually get used in practice**, with a vendored production stack you can copy into any project. It defers to the official docs for everything else.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants to track ML experiments (params, metrics, artifacts) with a UI
15	- User mentions `mlflow.start_run`, `mlflow.log_metric`, `mlflow.set_tracking_uri`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `mlflow ui`
16	- User wants framework autologging (sklearn / PyTorch / Lightning / XGBoost / LightGBM / Keras / TensorFlow / Transformers / spark)
17	- User wants LLM trace observability (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, AutoGen, CrewAI, etc.)
18	- User wants to spin up a self-hosted tracking server with PostgreSQL + MinIO (production)
19	- User wants a model registry with aliases (Champion / Challenger / Production)
20	- User asks "how do I compare runs", "where do my logged params go", "how do I serve a logged model"
21	
22	## When NOT to use
23	
24	- User wants reproducible **pipelines** with data versioning → use `dvc-ml-workflow` skill
25	- User wants Weights & Biases specifically → MLflow is the open-source counterpart but not a drop-in replacement
26	- User wants DataBricks-managed MLflow → most code transfers, but auth/workspace setup is Databricks-specific; defer to Databricks docs
27	- User wants a single throwaway run with no UI → `print()` is fine; MLflow adds overhead
28	
29	## Authoritative sources (link these, don't paraphrase from memory)
30	
31	- Docs root: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest
32	- Tracking: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracking.html
33	- Model Registry: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/model-registry.html
34	- LLM tracing / GenAI: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/llms/tracing/index.html
35	- Autologging matrix: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracking/autolog.html
36	- Upstream repo: https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow
37	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/mlflow/
38	- mlflow-widgets (anywidget for live charts): https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets
39	
40	MLflow ships a release roughly every 4–6 weeks. **Fetch the docs page** before answering version-specific questions (especially anything about LLM tracing, which is the fastest-moving area).
41	
42	## Decision: which deployment mode?
43	
44	Pick **before** writing any code. Switching later means migrating runs.
45	
46	| Mode | Tracking URI | When to choose | Read |
47	|---|---|---|---|
48	| **File** | `file:./mlruns` (default) | One-off experiments, no UI needed, no model registry | — |
49	| **SQLite + `mlflow ui`** ⭐ | `sqlite:///mlflow.db` | Solo work, small-to-medium experiment counts, want UI without running a server | `references/sqlite-local.md` |
50	| **Docker Compose stack** ⭐ | `http://host:8000` (PostgreSQL + MinIO) | Team use, production, parallel jobs, large artifacts, model registry across projects | `references/docker-compose-server.md` + `assets/docker-compose-stack/` |
51	| Databricks-managed | `databricks://` | Already paying for Databricks | (out of scope; defer to Databricks docs) |
52	
53	The two starred modes cover ~95% of real use. **Default**: SQLite for quick experiments, Docker Compose stack when more than one person needs to see the same runs.
54	
55	### File mode is for transient runs only
56	
57	The default `file:./mlruns` mode does NOT support the model registry — `mlflow.register_model()` raises. If the user wants a registry **at all**, they need SQLite or a server backend, even for solo use.
58	
59	## Workflow
60	
61	### 1. Initialize the chosen mode
62	
63	**SQLite (recommended for solo)**:
64	
65	```bash
66	bash skills/local/mlflow-tracking/scripts/init-mlflow-sqlite.sh
67	# Creates mlflow.db, .gitignore entries, prints the URL to launch `mlflow ui`
68	```
69	
70	**Docker Compose stack (recommended for team)**:
71	
72	```bash
73	bash skills/local/mlflow-tracking/scripts/start-mlflow-server.sh --target-dir infra/mlflow
74	# Copies assets/docker-compose-stack/ into infra/mlflow/, customizes .env,
75	# runs `docker compose up -d`, waits for the healthcheck, prints the URL.
76	```
77	
78	### 2. Set the tracking URI in your code
79	
80	```python
81	import mlflow
82	
83	# SQLite mode:
84	mlflow.set_tracking_uri("sqlite:///mlflow.db")
85	
86	# Server mode:
87	mlflow.set_tracking_uri("http://localhost:8000")
88	```
89	
90	Or via env var (preferred for subprocess / CI consistency):
91	
92	```bash
93	export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///mlflow.db
94	# or
95	export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://localhost:8000
96	```
97	
98	`set_tracking_uri()` only affects the current process. Subprocesses MUST use the env var.
99	
100	### 3. Log a run
101	
102	Two equally-valid styles. **Pick one**, don't mix in the same script.
103	
104	**Manual logging** (full control):
105	
106	```python
107	mlflow.set_experiment("my-project")           # creates if missing
108	
109	with mlflow.start_run(run_name="baseline"):
110	    mlflow.log_params({"lr": 1e-3, "epochs": 25})
111	    for epoch in range(25):
112	        loss = train_step()
113	        mlflow.log_metric("train_loss", loss, step=epoch)
114	    mlflow.log_artifact("config.yaml")
115	    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, "model")
116	```
117	
118	**Autologging** (zero-touch — preferred for supported frameworks):
119	
120	```python
121	import mlflow
122	mlflow.autolog()                              # detects framework at first .fit()
123	# OR explicit:
124	mlflow.sklearn.autolog()
125	mlflow.pytorch.autolog()
126	mlflow.transformers.autolog()
127	
128	with mlflow.start_run():
129	    model.fit(X, y)                           # params, metrics, model all logged
130	```
131	
132	For per-framework caveats and the full list of supported libraries, **read** `references/autologging-by-framework.md`.
133	
134	### 4. View results
135	
136	```bash
137	# SQLite mode — must pass the same URI explicitly:
138	mlflow ui --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db --port 5001
139	
140	# Server mode — already has a UI at http://localhost:8000
141	```
142	
143	For programmatic access:
144	
145	```python
146	runs = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=["my-project"])    # pandas DataFrame
147	best = runs.sort_values("metrics.val_acc", ascending=False).iloc[0]
148	```
149	
150	The bundled `scripts/tail-runs.sh` wraps `mlflow.search_runs` for terminal use.
151	
152	### 5. Promote a model with the registry
153	
154	```python
155	mlflow.set_registry_uri(mlflow.get_tracking_uri())   # usually unnecessary; auto-inherits
156	
157	# Register from a logged run:
158	result = mlflow.register_model(
159	    f"runs:/{run_id}/model",
160	    name="my-model",
161	)
162	
163	# Set an alias (replaces deprecated stages):
164	client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
165	client.set_registered_model_alias("my-model", "Champion", version=result.version)
166	
167	# Load by alias:
168	model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/my-model@Champion")
169	```
170	
171	For aliases vs deprecated stages, model versioning, and webhooks, **read** `references/model-registry.md`.
172	
173	### 6. (Optional) Trace LLM calls
174	
175	MLflow 2.14+ ships an OpenTelemetry-style tracing system that competes with W&B Weave / LangSmith / LangFuse:
176	
177	```python
178	import mlflow
179	mlflow.openai.autolog()         # auto-trace every OpenAI SDK call
180	# also: mlflow.anthropic / langchain / llama_index / dspy / autogen / crewai / litellm
181	
182	# Or manual spans:
183	@mlflow.trace
184	def my_chain(query):
185	    return rag(query)
186	```
187	
188	Traces show in the MLflow UI under the "Traces" tab. For provider matrix and trace querying, **read** `references/llm-tracing.md`.
189	
190	### 7. (Optional) Live charts in marimo / Jupyter
191	
192	Use `mlflow-widgets` (your own anywidget) for live-updating charts inside notebooks without spinning up the UI:
193	
194	```python
195	from mlflow_widgets import MlflowChart
196	MlflowChart(experiment_name="my-project", metric="val_loss")
197	```
198	
199	See `references/mlflow-widgets-anywidget.md` for installation and embedding patterns.
200	
201	## Available scripts
202	
203	- **`scripts/init-mlflow-sqlite.sh`** — Idempotent SQLite-mode init: touches `mlflow.db` if missing, adds `.gitignore` entries (`mlflow.db`, `mlruns/`, `mlartifacts/`), prints the exact `mlflow ui` command and `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` value to export.
204	  - Flags: `--db-path PATH` (default `mlflow.db`), `--port N` (default 5001), `--dry-run`, `--help`
205	- **`scripts/start-mlflow-server.sh`** — Copy `assets/docker-compose-stack/` into a target directory, generate `.env` from template (with secret rotation prompt), `docker compose up -d`, wait for healthcheck, print URLs.
206	  - Flags: `--target-dir DIR` (default `infra/mlflow`), `--port N` (default 8000), `--no-rotate-secrets`, `--dry-run`, `--help`
207	- **`scripts/tail-runs.sh`** — Wrap `mlflow.search_runs()` for terminal use. PEP 723 inline deps — runs via `uv run` with no setup. Outputs CSV/JSON to stdout.
208	  - Flags: `--experiment NAME`, `--top-n N`, `--sort-by METRIC`, `--format {json,csv}`, `--tracking-uri URI`, `--help`
209	
210	## Bundled assets
211	
212	- `assets/docker-compose-stack/` — Production-grade MLflow server: `docker-compose.yaml` (PostgreSQL + MinIO + tracking server + bucket bootstrap), `Dockerfile` (pinned MLflow image + psycopg2 + boto3), `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`. Copy the whole folder into `<project>/infra/mlflow/`.
213	
214	## Reference files
215	
216	- `references/sqlite-local.md` — Read **when** the user picks SQLite mode or asks about `mlflow ui` not finding their runs. Covers the explicit `--backend-store-uri` requirement (the #1 SQLite-mode confusion).
217	- `references/docker-compose-server.md` — Read **when** deploying the server stack: customizing `.env`, persisting `mlflow_data/`, securing MinIO, using AWS S3 instead of MinIO, fronting with nginx + auth.
218	- `references/llm-tracing.md` — Read **when** the user asks about LLM observability, traces, prompts, token costs, or any of: OpenAI / Anthropic / LangChain / LlamaIndex / DSPy / AutoGen / CrewAI / LiteLLM. Covers `mlflow.<provider>.autolog`, `@mlflow.trace`, span attributes, and trace search.
219	- `references/model-registry.md` — Read **when** the user wants to manage model versions, promote between environments, or asks about Champion/Challenger. Covers aliases (current API) vs stages (deprecated), `MlflowClient`, webhooks.
220	- `references/autologging-by-framework.md` — Read **when** picking autolog for a specific library. Covers all officially-supported frameworks (sklearn, pytorch, lightning, tensorflow, keras, xgboost, lightgbm, catboost, statsmodels, spark, fastai, gluon, paddle, transformers) with per-framework gotchas.
221	- `references/mlflow-widgets-anywidget.md` — Read **when** the user wants live charts inside marimo or Jupyter without launching the full MLflow UI. Covers installation, the `MlflowChart` API, and embedding patterns.
222	
223	## Gotchas
224	
225	- **`mlflow ui` does NOT auto-pick up `sqlite:///mlflow.db`.** It defaults to `./mlruns/`. You MUST pass `--backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db` (matching what your code uses) or you'll see an empty UI. The init script prints the right command.
226	- **`set_tracking_uri()` is process-local.** Subprocesses (e.g., `subprocess.run`, `joblib`, `multiprocessing`) won't inherit it unless you set `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` in the environment first.
227	- **Autolog must be called BEFORE `start_run()`** (or before the first `.fit()` if you're not using a context manager). Calling it after silently logs nothing.
228	- **Model registry requires a database backend**. `file:./mlruns` raises on `register_model`. SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL all work.
229	- **macOS port 5000 conflict**: AirPlay Receiver hijacks port 5000. The Docker stack uses 8000; the SQLite UI script uses 5001. If the user insists on 5000, tell them to disable AirPlay Receiver in System Settings → General → AirDrop & Handoff.
230	- **`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` must be set in the CLIENT environment** when using a server with S3/MinIO artifacts — the MLflow client uploads artifacts directly to S3, not via the server. Server-side env vars are not enough.
231	- **SQLite + parallel workers = `database is locked`.** SQLite serializes writes. Once the user is running >1 trainer at a time, migrate to the Docker stack (PostgreSQL).
232	- **Stages (`Staging` / `Production`) are deprecated** in MLflow ≥ 2.9. Use **aliases** (`Champion`, `Challenger`, etc.). Old code with `transition_model_version_stage()` still works but emits warnings; new code should use `set_registered_model_alias()`.
233	- **Run names are NOT unique** within an experiment. Two runs can both be named `"baseline"`. Identity = `run_id` (UUID). Set explicit, semantic `run_name` for human readability, but use `run_id` programmatically.
234	- **`MLFLOW_REGISTRY_URI` is almost never needed.** When tracking URI is HTTP / SQLite / PostgreSQL, the registry uses the same backend automatically. Setting both to different values is an advanced setup; don't do it by default.
235	
236	## Cross-references
237	
238	- For **marimo notebooks specifically** with a Tyro-based dual-mode (UI + batch CLI) pattern that uses MLflow, see the `marimo-batch-mlflow` skill — that one is a specialization, this skill is the general-purpose foundation.
239

1	# Agent skills (npx skills) cable channel for television (tv)
2	#
3	# Lists project-local + global agent skills via the `skills` npm package.
4	# Pairs with `skills-walk` (filesystem-only enumeration; no npx).
5	#
6	# Usage:
7	#   tv skills
8	#
9	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
10	#   1. Project + Global merged (default)  — combined view, [P]/[G] tag column
11	#   2. Project only                        — `npx skills list`
12	#   3. Global only                         — `npx skills list -g`
13	#
14	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
15	#   1. SKILL.md rendered with bat
16	#   2. Skill directory listing (eza/ls -la)
17	#
18	# Keybindings:
19	#   Enter      Show SKILL.md in $PAGER (less)
20	#   Alt+E      Open SKILL.md in $EDITOR
21	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy skill name to clipboard
22	#   Alt+P      Copy absolute path to clipboard
23	#   Alt+I      Print "skill: <name>" hint to stdout (for agent prompt paste)
24	#
25	# Ctrl+E is left as TV's global `go_to_input_end` — Alt+E for edit follows
26	# the same convention as the git-ops channel.
27	
28	[metadata]
29	name = "skills"
30	description = "Agent skills (npx skills) — project + global, preview SKILL.md, edit / copy"
31	requirements = ["npx", "bat"]
32	
33	[source]
34	# All three sources emit the same TSV columns:
35	#   0. scope tag    ([P] / [G])
36	#   1. skill name
37	#   2. absolute path (tilde-expanded)
38	#   3. agents string (e.g. "Claude Code, Codex, Cursor +3 more")
39	#
40	# `npx skills list` output format (after stripping ANSI):
41	#   <name> <path>            ← name + path on one line, separated by spaces
42	#     Agents: <comma-list>   ← indented continuation
43	#
44	# We strip ANSI with sed, then a state-machine awk pairs each name+path row
45	# with the next "Agents:" row.
46	command = [
47	  # Cycle 1: project + global merged.
48	  '''
49	  _parse() {
50	    tag="$1"; cmd="$2"
51	    eval "$cmd" 2>/dev/null \
52	      | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mK]//g' \
53	      | awk -v tag="$tag" '
54	          /^[[:space:]]*Agents:/ {
55	            sub(/^[[:space:]]*Agents:[[:space:]]*/, "")
56	            agents = $0
57	            if (name != "") {
58	              printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", tag, name, path, agents
59	              name = ""; path = ""; agents = ""
60	            }
61	            next
62	          }
63	          /^[[:space:]]*$/ || /^[[:space:]]*Project Skills/ || /^[[:space:]]*Global Skills/ { next }
64	          /^[^[:space:]]/ {
65	            # Flush previous (no Agents line)
66	            if (name != "") {
67	              printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", tag, name, path, "—"
68	            }
69	            # name is field 1, path is field 2 (rest)
70	            name = $1
71	            path = $2
72	            for (i = 3; i <= NF; i++) path = path " " $i
73	            # Expand leading ~ to $HOME for downstream tools
74	            sub(/^~/, ENVIRON["HOME"], path)
75	          }
76	          END {
77	            if (name != "") printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", tag, name, path, (agents == "" ? "—" : agents)
78	          }
79	        '
80	  }
81	  _parse "[P]" "npx --no-install skills list 2>/dev/null || npx skills list"
82	  _parse "[G]" "npx --no-install skills list -g 2>/dev/null || npx skills list -g"
83	  ''',
84	  # Cycle 2: project only.
85	  '''
86	  { npx --no-install skills list 2>/dev/null || npx skills list 2>/dev/null; } \
87	    | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mK]//g' \
88	    | awk '
89	        /^[[:space:]]*Agents:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*Agents:[[:space:]]*/, ""); agents=$0; if(name!="") {printf "[P]\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", name, path, agents; name=""; path=""; agents=""} next }
90	        /^[[:space:]]*$/ || /^[[:space:]]*Project Skills/ { next }
91	        /^[^[:space:]]/ {
92	          if (name != "") printf "[P]\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", name, path, "—"
93	          name=$1; path=$2; for(i=3;i<=NF;i++) path=path" "$i; sub(/^~/, ENVIRON["HOME"], path)
94	        }
95	        END { if(name!="") printf "[P]\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", name, path, (agents==""?"—":agents) }
96	      '
97	  ''',
98	  # Cycle 3: global only.
99	  '''
100	  { npx --no-install skills list -g 2>/dev/null || npx skills list -g 2>/dev/null; } \
101	    | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mK]//g' \
102	    | awk '
103	        /^[[:space:]]*Agents:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*Agents:[[:space:]]*/, ""); agents=$0; if(name!="") {printf "[G]\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", name, path, agents; name=""; path=""; agents=""} next }
104	        /^[[:space:]]*$/ || /^[[:space:]]*Global Skills/ { next }
105	        /^[^[:space:]]/ {
106	          if (name != "") printf "[G]\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", name, path, "—"
107	          name=$1; path=$2; for(i=3;i<=NF;i++) path=path" "$i; sub(/^~/, ENVIRON["HOME"], path)
108	        }
109	        END { if(name!="") printf "[G]\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", name, path, (agents==""?"—":agents) }
110	      '
111	  ''',
112	]

114	output = "{split:\t:1}"

## Television Channel Configuration Analysis

I've thoroughly explored the television (tv) channel configuration in your repo. Here's the complete pattern for designing an MLflow channel:

### 1. **General TOML Schema (Required & Optional Fields)**

Every channel follows this structure:

**Required sections:**
- `[metadata]` — name, description, optional requirements (tools needed)
- `[source]` — command(s) producing TSV/list output; display/output row format
- `[preview]` — command(s) for cycling preview views
- `[keybindings]` — optional custom key actions (defaults handled globally)
- `[actions.*]` — implementations of custom keybindings

**Key fields:**
- `command` — string or array (TSV output for source; plaintext/JSON for preview)
- `display` — how to format rows using `{split:\t:N}` or `{split:\<char>:N}` placeholders
- `output` — what gets emitted when Enter is pressed; also `{split:...}` syntax
- `watch` — seconds between auto-refresh (e.g., 2.0 for pueue, 5.0 for super-productivity)
- `no_sort` — true to prevent TV's default alphabetical sort
- `header` — preview title using placeholders

### 2. **Template Pattern (`.toml.tmpl` Files)**

Templates are used exclusively for **cross-platform conditionals** and **chezmoi data injection**:

- **`mac-procs.toml.tmpl`** — wrapped in `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}...{{ end -}}` (macOS only; Linux gets deleted)
- **`services.toml.tmpl`** — two complete source/action sets: one for Linux systemd, one for macOS launchd (same key names, different implementations)
- **`disk.toml.tmpl`**, **`users.toml.tmpl`**, **`scheduled-jobs.toml.tmpl`** — similar OS conditionals

**Not templated when:** channel is platform-agnostic (clash-api, pueue, super-productivity are all `.toml`).

For MLflow: use `.toml` unless your channel needs OS-specific behavior.

### 3. **Placeholder Syntax for Selected Items**

TV uses **field splitting + indexing**:
- `{split:\t:0}` — first field (source command splits on tab by default)
- `{split:\t:2}` — third field
- `{split: :0}` — first space-separated field (used in mac-procs for PID extraction)
- `{split:\\t:0}` — escaped in triple-quoted strings (prevents TOML parser from eating backslash)
- `{strip_ansi}` — remove ANSI color codes

**Important:** The comment in agent-sessions.toml warns: *"do NOT embed Python/awk/JSON literals inline here — any bare `{...}` (outside TV's own placeholders) silently breaks ALL placeholder substitution."*

### 4. **Runtime Configuration (Env Vars vs Hardcoding)**

**Existing patterns:**

- **`clash-api.toml`** — reads `$CLASH_CONTROLLER` and `$CLASH_SECRET` env vars, then delegates controller discovery to a helper script (`clash-source.sh`), which tries: explicit env → parsed YAML config (via `clash-parse.py`) → localhost 127.0.0.1:9090 as fallback.

- **`super-productivity.toml`** — hardcoded to `http://127.0.0.1:3876` (no env var override currently; the source helper reads it from the app's settings if needed). Note at top of the file says "requires desktop Electron app with Local REST API enabled."

**Recommendation for MLflow:** Follow clash-api pattern:
```bash
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-http://127.0.0.1:5000}"
```
This allows users to override at runtime while providing a sensible localhost default.

### 5. **Existing HTTP API Channels**

**`clash-api.toml`** (most relevant):
- Uses helper scripts: `clash-source.sh`, `clash-preview.sh`, `clash-parse.py`
- Source emits: kind (proxy/group/rule), name, metadata — TSV columns
- Preview cycles: JSON detail → latency probe → meta relationships
- Actions: `test_latency` (calls `/delay`), `switch_proxy`, `close_connections` (DELETE /connections), `reload_config` (PUT with JSON body)
- Requirements: curl, uv (for YAML parsing)

**`super-productivity.toml`** (simpler, best mimic):
- Direct `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/{id}` in preview command
- Source helper (shell script) handles preflight health check, caching, mode routing
- Output: TSV with id, marker (▶/✓/○), project, title
- Actions: open-detail (jq pretty), copy-id, copy-title, dump-json
- Requirements: curl, jq

**`pueue.toml`** (JSON-heavy):
- Source pipes `pueue status --json` to jq for filtering
- Two action hooks: `reload_source` (implicit `ctrl-r`) after mutations to refresh
- Demonstrates keybinding chains: `alt-p = ["actions:pause", "reload_source"]`

### 6. **Cleanest Example to Mimic: `super-productivity.toml`**

```toml
[metadata]
name = "super-productivity"
description = "Super Productivity (read-only): browse tasks, projects, tags via local REST API"
requirements = ["curl", "jq"]

[source]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-active",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-all",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-archived",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh projects",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tags",
]
display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:1}  [{split:\t:2}]  {split:\t:3}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"
watch = 5.0
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data || echo 'No JSON detail for this row (project/tag entries do not have a /tasks/:id endpoint, or API is unreachable).'",
  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.data.notes // \"(no notes)\"' || echo '(no notes available)'",
]
header = "{split:\t:1}  {split:\t:3}"

[ui]
input_header = "Super Productivity"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open-detail"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
alt-y = "actions:copy-title"

[actions.open-detail]
description = "Open full JSON detail in pager"
command = "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-id]
description = "Copy row id to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"
```

**Why this is cleanest:**
- No `.tmpl` (platform-agnostic)
- Helper script handles health checks + error messaging (keeps TOML lean)
- Source cycles via array of commands (Ctrl+S toggles)
- Preview cycles via array too (Ctrl+F)
- Actions clearly separated (`mode: "execute"` for interactive, `mode: "fork"` for async)
- Requirements declared upfront
- Tab-delimited TSV (simpler than jq pipes in source)

---

**File paths for reference:**
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/super-productivity.toml` — full template
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_super-productivity-source.sh` — example helper
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/config.toml` — global TV settings
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/clash-api.toml` — advanced (env vars, auth headers)
```

363	header = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:2}  ({split:\t:3})"

371	[keybindings]
372	enter = "actions:print_resume"
373	alt-t = "actions:resume"
374	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
375	alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"
376	alt-r = "actions:copy_resume"

378	alt-e = "actions:edit_jsonl"

380	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
381	# Helper: assemble the agent-specific resume invocation.
382	# Each action sources `_resume_cmd` to keep the per-agent mapping in one place.
383	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
384	[actions.print_resume]
385	description = "Print 'cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>' to stdout"
386	command = '''
387	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'
388	case "$agent" in
389	  "[oc]") cmd="opencode --session $sid" ;;
390	  "[cc]") cmd="claude --resume $sid" ;;
391	  "[cx]") cmd="codex resume $sid" ;;
392	  "[cu]") cmd="cursor-agent --resume $sid" ;;
393	  "[ci]") cmd="cursor   # IDE composer $sid (open from sidebar)" ;;
394	esac
395	case "$dir" in
396	  /*) printf 'cd %q && %s\n' "$dir" "$cmd" ;;
397	  vscode-remote://*) printf '%s   # remote: %s\n' "$cmd" "$dir" ;;
398	  *)  printf '%s   # cwd: %s\n' "$cmd" "$dir" ;;
399	esac
400	'''
401	mode = "execute"
402	
403	[actions.resume]
404	description = "cd to session dir and resume agent (in current terminal)"
405	command = '''
406	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'
407	case "$dir" in /*) cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null || { echo "cd failed: $dir"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 1; } ;; esac
408	case "$agent" in
409	  "[oc]") exec opencode --session "$sid" ;;
410	  "[cc]") exec claude --resume "$sid" ;;
411	  "[cx]") exec codex resume "$sid" ;;
412	  "[cu]") exec cursor-agent --resume "$sid" ;;
413	  "[ci]")
414	    case "$dir" in
415	      /*) exec cursor "$dir" ;;
416	      vscode-remote://*) echo "Remote workspace: $dir"; echo "Composer ID: $sid"; echo "Open Cursor and pick this chat from the sidebar."; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
417	      *) echo "Unknown workspace: $dir"; echo "Composer ID: $sid"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
418	    esac
419	    ;;
420	esac
421	'''
422	mode = "execute"
423	
424	[actions.copy_id]
425	description = "Copy session ID to clipboard"
426	command = '''
427	d='{split:\t:2}'
428	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
429	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
430	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
431	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
432	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
433	fi
434	'''
435	mode = "fork"
436	
437	[actions.copy_dir]
438	description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
439	command = '''
440	d='{split:\t:3}'
441	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
442	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
443	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
444	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
445	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
446	fi
447	'''
448	mode = "fork"
449	
450	[actions.copy_specstory]
451	description = "Copy .specstory/history/*.md path to clipboard (SpecStory reverse-lookup)"
452	command = '''
453	d='{split:\t:5}'
454	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
455	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
456	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
457	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
458	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
459	fi
460	'''
461	mode = "fork"
462	
463	[actions.copy_resume]
464	description = "Copy 'cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>' to clipboard"
465	command = '''
466	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'
467	case "$agent" in
468	  "[oc]") cmd="opencode --session $sid" ;;
469	  "[cc]") cmd="claude --resume $sid" ;;
470	  "[cx]") cmd="codex resume $sid" ;;
471	  "[cu]") cmd="cursor-agent --resume $sid" ;;
472	  "[ci]") cmd="cursor $dir" ;;
473	esac
474	case "$dir" in
475	  /*) [ "$agent" = "[ci]" ] && line="$cmd" || line=$(printf 'cd %q && %s' "$dir" "$cmd") ;;
476	  *)  line="$cmd" ;;
477	esac
478	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$line" | pbcopy
479	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$line" | wl-copy
480	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$line" | xclip -selection clipboard
481	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$line" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
482	fi
483	'''
484	mode = "fork"
485	
486	[actions.edit_jsonl]
487	description = "Open raw session file in $EDITOR (claude/codex only)"
488	command = '''
489	agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'
490	case "$agent" in
491	  "[cc]") f=$(find "$HOME/.claude/projects" -name "${sid}.jsonl" -not -path "*/subagents/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1) ;;
492	  "[cx]") f=$(find "$HOME/.codex/sessions" -name "rollout-*${sid}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | head -1) ;;
493	  "[oc]") echo "OpenCode sessions live in SQLite — use 'opencode export $sid' instead."; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
494	  "[cu]") echo "Cursor sessions live in opaque BLOBs — no plaintext to edit."; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
495	  "[ci]") echo "Cursor IDE chats live in state.vscdb (cursorDiskKV table) — no plaintext to edit."; echo "Composer ID: $sid"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0 ;;
496	esac
497	if [ -z "$f" ] || [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
498	  echo "Session file not found for $sid"; echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _; exit 0
499	fi
500	"${EDITOR:-vi}" "$f"
501	'''

```text
1	# Pueue task manager channel for television (tv)
2	# Fuzzy-search pueue tasks, preview logs, and manage tasks interactively.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   tv pueue
6	#
7	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
8	#   1. All tasks (newest first)
9	#   2. Active only (Running + Queued + Paused)
10	#   3. Failed only
11	#   4. Groups overview
12	#
13	# Keybindings (Alt+key avoids conflicts with TV built-ins and tmux):
14	#   Enter      Follow running task / view finished task log / show group status
15	#   Alt+E      Edit task command (stashed/queued only, opens $EDITOR)
16	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy raw command to clipboard (overrides TV default; OSC 52 over SSH)
17	#   Alt+Y      Copy raw command to clipboard (same as Ctrl+Y)
18	#   Alt+A      Copy full `pueue add ...` command to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)
19	#   Alt+G      Filter by group (opens new tv with only that group's tasks)
20	#   Alt+P      Pause task
21	#   Alt+R      Resume (start) task
22	#   Alt+K      Kill task
23	#   Alt+T      Restart task (in-place)
24	#   Alt+X      Remove task
25	#   Alt+L      Clean all finished tasks
26	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (log output / JSON details)
27	#   Ctrl+O     Toggle preview panel
28	#
29	# Auto-refreshes every 2 seconds via watch mode.
30	
31	[metadata]
32	name = "pueue"
33	description = "Pueue task manager: search, preview logs, pause/resume/kill/restart"
34	requirements = ["pueue", "jq"]
35	
36	[source]
37	command = [
38	  """pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tasks | to_entries | sort_by(.value.id | tonumber) | reverse | .[].value | (if .status == "Queued" then "\u23f3 Queued" elif .status == "Stashed" then "\u23f9 Stashed" elif (.status | type == "object") then if (.status | has("Running")) then "\u25b6 Running" elif (.status | has("Done")) then if .status.Done.result == "Success" then "\u2713 Done" else "\u2717 Failed" end elif (.status | has("Paused")) then "\u23f8 Paused" else (.status | keys[0]) end else (.status | tostring) end) as $st | [(.id | tostring), $st, .group, .original_command] | @tsv'""",
39	  """pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tasks | to_entries | sort_by(.value.id | tonumber) | reverse | .[].value | select(.status == "Queued" or (.status | type == "object" and (has("Running") or has("Paused")))) | (if .status == "Queued" then "\u23f3 Queued" elif (.status | has("Running")) then "\u25b6 Running" elif (.status | has("Paused")) then "\u23f8 Paused" else (.status | keys[0]) end) as $st | [(.id | tostring), $st, .group, .original_command] | @tsv'""",
40	  """pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.tasks | to_entries | sort_by(.value.id | tonumber) | reverse | .[].value | select(.status | type == "object" and has("Done") and .status.Done.result != "Success") | [(.id | tostring), "\u2717 Failed", .group, .original_command] | @tsv'""",
41	  """pueue group --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, .value.status, ("parallel=" + (.value.parallel_tasks | tostring))] | @tsv'""",
42	]
43	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  [{split:\\t:2}]  {split:\\t:3}"
44	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
45	watch = 2.0
46	no_sort = true
47	
48	[preview]
49	# Preview cycle 1 pipes pueue log output through `tspin --print` when tailspin
50	# is installed, for colorful highlighting of timestamps/levels/IPs/URLs in the

1	# Live Clash / mihomo controller channel for television (tv).
2	# Fuzzy-search the external-controller API directly: proxies, proxy groups,
3	# rules, and runtime summary rows from /version, /configs, and /connections.
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv clash-api
7	#   CLASH_CONTROLLER=192.168.222.207:9090 tv clash-api
8	#   CLASH_CONTROLLER=192.168.222.207:9090 CLASH_SECRET=mytoken tv clash-api
9	#
10	# Controller discovery:
11	#   $CLASH_CONTROLLER / $CLASH_SECRET           (explicit override)
12	#   runtime external-controller from local Clash config
13	#   reachable Docker/local controller at 127.0.0.1:9090
14	#
15	# Prereqs: `curl`. `uv` is optional here: it is only used when no controller
16	# env vars are set and the helper falls back to the local YAML config.
17	#
18	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
19	#   1. Proxies              live /proxies leaf entries
20	#   2. Proxy Groups         live /proxies selector/url-test/fallback entries
21	#   3. Rules                live /rules entries
22	#   4. Summary              /version + /configs + /connections
23	#
24	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):

27	#   3. Meta      proxy-group references, group members, nearby rules

104	if [ -z "${host:-}" ]; then

127	if [ -z "${host:-}" ]; then

129	  sleep 1
130	  exit 0
131	fi
132	cfg_path="${CLASH_CONFIG:-}"
133	if [ -z "${cfg_path:-}" ]; then

135	fi
136	if [ -z "${cfg_path:-}" ]; then

138	  sleep 1
139	  exit 0
140	fi
141	if [ -n "${CLASH_CONTROLLER:-}" ] && [ -z "${CLASH_CONFIG:-}" ]; then

151	printf 'Reload %s via %s? [y/N]: ' "$cfg_path" "$host"
152	read -r confirm
153	case "$confirm" in y|Y|yes|YES) ;; *) echo 'aborted'; sleep 1; exit 0 ;; esac
154	rc=$(curl -sS -o /tmp/clash-reload.out -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 -X PUT \\
155	  "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
156	  -d "$(python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.dumps({"path": sys.argv[1]}))' "$cfg_path")" \\
157	  "http://$host/configs?force=true" 2>/dev/null || true)
158	case "$rc" in

160	  *)  printf 'Reload failed (HTTP %s):\\n%s\\n' "$rc" "$(cat /tmp/clash-reload.out 2>/dev/null)" ;;

1	# Super Productivity channel for television (tv).
2	# Read-only browser for tasks, projects and tags via SP's local REST API
3	# (http://127.0.0.1:3876, exposed by the desktop Electron app).
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv super-productivity
7	#
8	# Prerequisites (one-time):
9	#   1. Super Productivity desktop ≥ 18.0.0 (the Local REST API was added in
10	#      upstream PR #6981, first shipped 2026-03-26). The Brewfile cask gets
11	#      the latest, but if you have an older install pinned, run:
12	#        brew upgrade --cask super-productivity
13	#      Confirm with: defaults read "/Applications/Super Productivity.app/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString
14	#   2. In the app: Settings → Misc → enable "Local REST API"
15	#      (NOT in Sync & Export — that section only configures Dropbox/WebDAV/
16	#      SuperSync data sync, which is independent of the REST API.)
17	#   3. Restart the app
18	#
19	# Verify the API is up:
20	#   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3876/health | jq
21	#   # -> {"ok":true,"data":{"server":"up","rendererReady":true}}
22	#
23	# When the API is unreachable, this channel shows a single hint row instead
24	# of an empty list — so you always know whether SP is the problem or `tv` is.
25	#
26	# Reverse-engineered route reference + design rationale:
27	#   docs/tools/super-productivity.md
28	#
29	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
30	#   1. Active tasks      open tasks excluding done (▶ marks current)
31	#   2. All active tasks  open + done tasks (✓ marks done)
32	#   3. Archived tasks    moved-to-archive tasks
33	#   4. Projects          all projects with task counts
34	#   5. Tags              all tags
35	#
36	# Preview cycle (Ctrl+F):
37	#   1. Full task JSON (jq-pretty)
38	#   2. Notes only (tspin-highlighted when tailspin is installed)
39	#
40	# Keybindings (read-only by design — no mutations in v0.1):
41	#   Enter      Open full JSON detail in pager
42	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy task ID to clipboard (overrides TV default)
43	#   Alt+Y      Copy task title to clipboard
44	#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal
45	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
46	#   Ctrl+O     Toggle preview panel
47	#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
48	#
49	# Refresh: every 5s (less aggressive than pueue's 2s — task data changes
50	# slowly and the renderer round-trip is heavier than a local CLI call).
51	#
52	# NOTE on Phase 2 (mutations): start/stop/complete/archive via Alt-keys is
53	# intentionally deferred until the read-only flow proves stable. The REST
54	# API supports them today (POST /tasks/:id/start, POST /task-control/stop,
55	# PATCH /tasks/:id with {isDone:true}, POST /tasks/:id/archive).
56	
57	[metadata]
58	name = "super-productivity"
59	description = "Super Productivity (read-only): browse tasks, projects, tags via local REST API"
60	requirements = ["curl", "jq"]
61	
62	[source]
63	command = [
64	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-active",
65	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-all",
66	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-archived",
67	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh projects",
68	  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tags",
69	]
70	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  [{split:\\t:2}]  {split:\\t:3}"
71	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
72	watch = 5.0
73	no_sort = true
74	
75	[preview]
76	# GET /tasks/:id only resolves for task ids — for project/tag rows the curl
77	# returns 404 and we fall back to a friendly message. Same for the down-API
78	# hint row (id "0"). All API responses are wrapped in {ok, data} — extract
79	# .data for display. Use `jq -C` for built-in syntax coloring (single binary,
80	# avoids `bat` PATH/TTY-detection gotchas inside TV's preview process).
81	command = [
82	  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data || echo 'No JSON detail for this row (project/tag entries do not have a /tasks/:id endpoint, or API is unreachable).'",
83	  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.data.notes // \"(no notes)\"' || echo '(no notes available)'",
84	]
85	header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"
86	
87	[ui]

96	ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"

98	alt-j = "actions:dump-json"
99	
100	[actions.open-detail]

102	command = "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
103	mode = "execute"

1	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
2	# mac-procs channel for television (tv) — macOS-only
3	# Fuzzy-pick the heaviest processes by memory (compressed-aware), with
4	# previews showing per-process VM map and open files.
5	#
6	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/55_macos_mem.sh.tmpl (mac-mem-*)
7	#             docs/tools/macos-swap.md (full deep-dive)
8	#
9	# Why this exists vs the generic kill-process channel:
10	#   - kill-process sorts by RSS (ps -axm). On Apple Silicon, RSS does
11	#     NOT include compressed or swapped pages — a process leaking 2 GB
12	#     of compressed data shows as 100 MB in RSS view.
13	#   - This channel uses `top -l 1 -o mem`, whose mem column matches
14	#     Activity Monitor's "Memory" column (compressed-aware).
15	#   - Per-PID preview uses `vmmap -summary` for the VM region breakdown
16	#     ps cannot show. (Apple Silicon also has `footprint -p PID` but it
17	#     needs sudo to inspect other users' processes.)
18	#
19	# No Alt-key bindings yet — user wanted to start with Enter only, add
20	# shortcuts after evaluating which actions are actually used. When
21	# ready, candidates: Alt+K (kill -TERM), Alt+9 (kill -9), Alt+I
22	# (footprint), Alt+V (vmmap full). Check AGENTS.md "Keyboard shortcuts"
23	# matrix before claiming any new Alt slot.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   tv mac-procs
27	#
28	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
29	#   1. Top by Memory (compressed-aware, default) — matches Activity Monitor
30	#   2. Top by CPU                                — what's burning the fan
31	#   3. Top by virtual size (ps -axm)             — fragmented apps / Electron
32	#
33	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
34	#   1. vmmap -summary  — VM region breakdown (no sudo)
35	#   2. ps metadata     — pid/ppid/user/etime/state/full command
36	#   3. lsof head       — top open files / sockets
37	
38	[metadata]
39	name = "mac-procs"
40	description = "macOS process picker — sorted by compressed-aware memory (top -o mem)"
41	requirements = []
42	
43	[source]
44	command = [
45	  # Cycle 1: top by Memory (compressed-aware). Default. PID is field 1.
46	  '''
47	  top -l 1 -o mem -n 30 -stats pid,command,mem,cpu,threads,state 2>/dev/null \
48	    | awk '/^PID/ {found=1; next}
49	           found==1 && NF>=5 {
50	               pid=$1; mem=$(NF-3); cpu=$(NF-2); thr=$(NF-1); st=$NF;
51	               cmd=""; for (i=2;i<=NF-4;i++) cmd=cmd" "$i; sub(/^ /, "", cmd);
52	               if (length(cmd) > 35) cmd=substr(cmd,1,32)"...";
53	               printf "%-7s  %-35s  MEM %8s  CPU %5s%%  TH %4s  %s\n", pid, cmd, mem, cpu, thr, st;
54	           }'
55	  ''',
56	  # Cycle 2: top by CPU. -l 2 because the first sample of `top -o cpu` is
57	  # since-boot and useless; the second sample is the actual delta.
58	  '''
59	  top -l 2 -o cpu -n 30 -stats pid,command,mem,cpu,threads,state 2>/dev/null \
60	    | awk '/^PID/ {found++; if(found==2) p=1; next}
61	           p==1 && NF>=5 {
62	               pid=$1; mem=$(NF-3); cpu=$(NF-2); thr=$(NF-1); st=$NF;
63	               cmd=""; for (i=2;i<=NF-4;i++) cmd=cmd" "$i; sub(/^ /, "", cmd);
64	               if (length(cmd) > 35) cmd=substr(cmd,1,32)"...";
65	               printf "%-7s  %-35s  MEM %8s  CPU %5s%%  TH %4s  %s\n", pid, cmd, mem, cpu, thr, st;
66	           }'
67	  ''',
68	  # Cycle 3: top by virtual size via ps. Catches Electron / fragmented apps
69	  # whose VSZ dwarfs their compressed-aware mem.
70	  '''
71	  ps -axm -o pid,vsz,rss,comm 2>/dev/null \
72	    | awk 'NR==1 {next}
73	           NR<=31 {
74	               pid=$1; vsz=$2/1024; rss=$3/1024;
75	               cmd=$4; for (i=5;i<=NF;i++) cmd=cmd" "$i;
76	               n=split(cmd,a,"/"); short=a[n];
77	               if (length(short) > 35) short=substr(short,1,32)"...";
78	               printf "%-7s  %-35s  VSZ %7.0fMB  RSS %7.0fMB\n", pid, short, vsz, rss;
79	           }'
80	  ''',
81	]
82	
83	[preview]
84	command = [
85	  # Cycle 1: vmmap -summary. Always available without sudo for own-uid procs;
86	  # for system procs you'll see "(parent's information not available)" — fine.
87	  "vmmap -summary '{split: :0}' 2>/dev/null | head -80",
88	  # Cycle 2: ps metadata in long form.
89	  "ps -p '{split: :0}' -o pid,ppid,user,pgid,%cpu,%mem,etime,state,command 2>/dev/null",
90	  # Cycle 3: lsof head — open files / sockets. Truncate to keep preview fast.
91	  "lsof -p '{split: :0}' 2>/dev/null | head -40",
92	]
93	
94	[keybindings]
95	# Enter: select_passthrough emits the current row to stdout, so users can
96	# pipe into other commands (e.g. `kill $(tv mac-procs | awk '{print $1}')`).
97	# No Alt-key actions yet — see file header for rationale and future
98	# candidates.
99	{{ end -}}
100
```

1	# services channel for television (tv) — cross-platform
2	# Fuzzy-browse systemd units on Linux / launchd jobs on macOS, with tailspin-
3	# colored log preview and Alt-key lifecycle actions.
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv services
7	#
8	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
9	#   1. Running only      — currently active services (system + user merged)
10	#   2. All loaded        — active + inactive + failed among *loaded* units
11	#   3. Failed only       — crashed / non-zero exit
12	#   4. User-scope only   — systemctl --user / macOS gui/$UID domain
13	#   5. Installed on-disk — every unit file / .plist on disk, with enablement badge
14	#      (catches "configured but not enabled" — land on a "○ Disabled" row and hit Alt+L)
15	#
16	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
17	#   1. Colorful log tail via tailspin (journalctl on Linux, StdoutPath / log show on macOS)
18	#   2. Status / details                (systemctl status / launchctl print)
19	#
20	# Keybindings:
21	#   Enter      Follow live log   (journalctl -fu / tail -F StdoutPath | tspin)
22	#   Alt+R      Restart           (sudo-aware when scope=system)
23	#   Alt+S      Stop
24	#   Alt+T      Start             (macOS: kickstart for loaded, bootstrap-by-search otherwise)
25	#   Alt+U      Reload            (systemctl reload-or-restart / launchctl kickstart)
26	#   Alt+D      Show status       (full pager — systemctl status / launchctl print)
27	#   Alt+E      Edit unit/plist   ($EDITOR on the unit file)
28	#   Alt+L      Toggle enable-on-boot (enable <-> disable)
29	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy name to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH)
30	#
31	# Rendered from services.toml.tmpl by chezmoi — macOS and Linux get different
32	# source/preview/action bodies. Template conditionals wrap per-OS branches.
33	
34	[metadata]
35	name = "services"
36	description = "Services: systemd (Linux) / launchd (macOS) — list, preview log, start/stop/restart/enable"
37	requirements = []
38	
39	[source]
40	command = [
41	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" }}
42	  # Cycle 1: Running only (system + user merged).
43	  '''
44	  for s in system user; do
45	    [ "$s" = system ] && cmd='systemctl' || cmd='systemctl --user'
46	    $cmd list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend --plain --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
47	      | awk -v scope="$s" '{u=$1;d="";for(i=5;i<=NF;i++)d=d (i>5?" ":"") $i;printf "▶ Running\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",u,scope,d}'
48	  done
49	  ''',
50	  # Cycle 2: All loaded (active + inactive + failed).
51	  '''
52	  for s in system user; do
53	    [ "$s" = system ] && cmd='systemctl' || cmd='systemctl --user'
54	    $cmd list-units --type=service --all --no-legend --plain --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
55	      | awk -v scope="$s" '{u=$1;a=$3;sb=$4;d="";for(i=5;i<=NF;i++)d=d (i>5?" ":"") $i; sym="? Unknown"; if(a=="active"&&sb=="running")sym="▶ Running"; else if(a=="active")sym="▶ Running"; else if(a=="failed")sym="✗ Failed"; else if(a=="inactive")sym="⏸ Stopped"; else if(a=="activating"||a=="deactivating")sym="… Transitioning"; printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",sym,u,scope,d}'
56	  done
57	  ''',
58	  # Cycle 3: Failed only.
59	  '''
60	  for s in system user; do
61	    [ "$s" = system ] && cmd='systemctl' || cmd='systemctl --user'
62	    $cmd list-units --type=service --state=failed --no-legend --plain --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
63	      | awk -v scope="$s" '{u=$1;d="";for(i=5;i<=NF;i++)d=d (i>5?" ":"") $i;printf "✗ Failed\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",u,scope,d}'
64	  done
65	  ''',
66	  # Cycle 4: User-scope only.
67	  '''
68	  systemctl --user list-units --type=service --all --no-legend --plain --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
69	    | awk -v scope=user '{u=$1;a=$3;sb=$4;d="";for(i=5;i<=NF;i++)d=d (i>5?" ":"") $i; sym="? Unknown"; if(a=="active"&&sb=="running")sym="▶ Running"; else if(a=="active")sym="▶ Running"; else if(a=="failed")sym="✗ Failed"; else if(a=="inactive")sym="⏸ Stopped"; else if(a=="activating"||a=="deactivating")sym="… Transitioning"; printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",sym,u,scope,d}'
70	  ''',

74	  for s in system user; do

77	      | awk -v scope="$s" '{u=$1;st=$2; sym="? Unknown"; if(st=="enabled")sym="✓ Enabled"; else if(st=="enabled-runtime")sym="✓ Enabled(rt)"; else if(st=="disabled")sym="○ Disabled"; else if(st=="static")sym="— Static"; else if(st=="masked")sym="⊘ Masked"; else if(st=="masked-runtime")sym="⊘ Masked(rt)"; else if(st=="alias")sym="↪ Alias"; else if(st=="indirect")sym="● Indirect"; else if(st=="generated")sym="⚙ Generated"; else if(st=="transient")sym="◌ Transient"; printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",sym,u,scope,st}'
78	  done
79	  ''',
80	{{- else if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }}
81	  # Cycle 1: Running only. `launchctl list` without sudo is gui/$UID domain;
82	  # with passwordless sudo we also merge system daemons.
83	  '''
84	  launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=user 'NR>1 && $1!="-" && $1!="PID" {printf "▶ Running\t%s\t%s\tPID=%s\n",$3,scope,$1}'
85	  if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
86	    sudo -n launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=system 'NR>1 && $1!="-" && $1!="PID" {printf "▶ Running\t%s\t%s\tPID=%s\n",$3,scope,$1}'
87	  fi
88	  ''',
89	  # Cycle 2: All loaded (running + stopped + failed).
90	  '''
91	  launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=user 'NR>1 && $3!="" && $1!="PID" {sym="? Unknown"; if($1!="-")sym="▶ Running"; else if($2+0!=0)sym="✗ Failed"; else sym="⏸ Stopped"; info=($1!="-"?"PID="$1:"exit="$2); printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",sym,$3,scope,info}'
92	  if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
93	    sudo -n launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=system 'NR>1 && $3!="" && $1!="PID" {sym="? Unknown"; if($1!="-")sym="▶ Running"; else if($2+0!=0)sym="✗ Failed"; else sym="⏸ Stopped"; info=($1!="-"?"PID="$1:"exit="$2); printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",sym,$3,scope,info}'
94	  else
95	    echo "ℹ Info\t(run: sudo -v to include system daemons)\tsystem\tpasswordless sudo required"
96	  fi
97	  ''',
98	  # Cycle 3: Failed only.
99	  '''
100	  launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=user 'NR>1 && $1=="-" && $2+0!=0 && $3!="" {printf "✗ Failed\t%s\t%s\texit=%s\n",$3,scope,$2}'
101	  if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
102	    sudo -n launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=system 'NR>1 && $1=="-" && $2+0!=0 && $3!="" {printf "✗ Failed\t%s\t%s\texit=%s\n",$3,scope,$2}'
103	  fi
104	  ''',
105	  # Cycle 4: User-scope only.
106	  '''
107	  launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk -v scope=user 'NR>1 && $3!="" && $1!="PID" {sym="? Unknown"; if($1!="-")sym="▶ Running"; else if($2+0!=0)sym="✗ Failed"; else sym="⏸ Stopped"; info=($1!="-"?"PID="$1:"exit="$2); printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",sym,$3,scope,info}'
108	  ''',
109	  # Cycle 5: Installed on-disk — scan admin-installed + user plist dirs.
110	  # Excludes /System/Library/Launch* to avoid ~600 Apple rows; edit this line
111	  # to opt-in by adding those paths.
112	  '''
113	  loaded=$(launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $3!="" && $1!="PID" {print $3}' | sort -u)

115	    [ -d "$p" ] || continue

121	      /Library/LaunchAgents/*)  scope=system ;;
122	      "$HOME"/Library/LaunchAgents/*) scope=user ;;
123	      *) scope=unknown ;;

129	    fi
130	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$sym" "$label" "$scope" "$plist"
131	  done
132	  ''',
133	{{- end }}

1	# Git operations cable channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/git-ops.md at runtime — single source of truth.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   tv git-ops                             (standalone: Enter prints, Ctrl+Y copies, Alt+E execs)
6	#   Alt+I in zsh                           (ZLE widget: pastes selected command into LBUFFER)
7	#
8	# Keybindings:
9	#   Enter      Print command to stdout (default; captured by Alt+I ZLE widget)
10	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy command to clipboard (overrides TV default; pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip/OSC 52)
11	#   Alt+E      Confirm then execute the command
12	#              (Ctrl+E is intentionally left as TV's global `go_to_input_end`)
13	#   Ctrl+O     Toggle preview panel (TV global)
14	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (markdown row ↔ `git help` page)
15	#
16	# Source format (TSV columns):
17	#   0. command    (raw; what gets printed / copied / executed)
18	#   1. label      (human-readable menu name matching VSCode/GitLens)
19	#   2. description
20	#   3. tag        ("⚠" for destructive, " " otherwise)
21	#   4. alias      (padded 10ch; oh-my-zsh git alias or *custom — searchable via fuzzy)
22	
23	[metadata]
24	name = "git-ops"
25	description = "VSCode + GitLens Git operations: search, paste, copy, or exec"
26	requirements = ["awk", "git"]
27	
28	[source]
29	command = """
30	awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|/ && $3 ~ /`/ {
31	  label=$2; cmd=$3; alias_=$4; desc=$5; notes=$6
32	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", label)
33	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", alias_)
34	  gsub(/`/, "", alias_)
35	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", desc)
36	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", notes)
37	  sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/, "", cmd); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/, "", cmd)
38	  tag = (notes ~ /destructive/) ? "⚠" : " "
39	  aliaspad = sprintf("%-11s", alias_)
40	  printf "%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n", cmd, label, desc, tag, aliaspad
41	}' ~/.config/docs/tools/git-ops.md
42	"""
43	display = "{split:\\t:3} {split:\\t:4} {split:\\t:1}  │  {split:\\t:0}  │  {split:\\t:2}"
44	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
45	
46	[preview]
47	command = [
48	  """label='{split:\\t:1}'; awk -v L="$label" 'BEGIN{FS="|"} $0 ~ "^\\\\| *"L" *\\\\|" {print; getline; print; exit}' ~/.config/docs/tools/git-ops.md | bat -l md --plain --color=always 2>/dev/null || awk -v L="$label" 'BEGIN{FS="|"} $0 ~ "^\\\\| *"L" *\\\\|" {print}' ~/.config/docs/tools/git-ops.md""",
49	  """cmd='{split:\\t:0}'; sub=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | awk '{print $2}'); git help "$sub" 2>/dev/null | head -80 || printf 'No help page for: %s\\n' "$cmd" """,
50	]
51	header = "{split:\\t:4} {split:\\t:1}"
52	
53	[ui.preview_panel]
54	size = 55
55	
56	[keybindings]

58	# Alt+E chosen for exec so we keep TV's global ctrl-e = go_to_input_end.
59	ctrl-y = "actions:copy"
60	alt-e = "actions:exec"
61	
62	[actions.copy]

64	command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
65	mode = "fork"

[y/N]: '; read -r ans; case "$ans" in y|Y|yes|YES) eval "$cmd" ;; *) printf 'Aborted.\\n' ;; esac; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""

1	# Custom keybindings cable channel for television (tv)

3	# the `bindings` shell function: ~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md
4	#
5	# Format contract (enforced by the picker too): every row is
6	#   | `<KEY>` | `<widget>` | <description> |
7	# parsed by awk -F'|' on lines that start with `| \``.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv keybindings                          (CLI)
11	#   bindings                                (shell function fallback)
12	#   Alt+/                                   (ZLE widget — the canonical entry)
13	#
14	# Keybindings inside the picker:
15	#   Enter      Paste "# <key> → <widget>: <desc>" comment
16	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the key combo to clipboard
17	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel (live `bindkey` lookup + source grep)
18	
19	[metadata]
20	name = "keybindings"
21	description = "Zsh keybindings cheatsheet: search built-in / plugin / custom widgets"
22	
23	[source]
24	command = """
25	awk -F'|' '
26	    /^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
27	        key=$2; widget=$3; desc=$4
28	        for (i in arr) delete arr[i]
29	        n = split("key widget desc", arr, " ")
30	        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
31	            v = (arr[i] == "key") ? key : (arr[i] == "widget") ? widget : desc
32	            gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
33	            gsub(/^`|`$/, "", v)
34	            if (arr[i] == "key")    key = v
35	            if (arr[i] == "widget") widget = v
36	            if (arr[i] == "desc")   desc = v
37	        }
38	        if (key == "Key" || key ~ /^-+$/) next
39	        if (key == "<KEY>") next
40	        printf "%-16s  %-32s  %s\\n", key, widget, desc
41	    }
42	' ~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md
43	"""
44	
45	[preview]
46	command = """
47	key=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $1}')
48	widget=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $2}')
49	echo "Key:    $key"
50	echo "Widget: $widget"
51	echo
52	echo '── Live bindkey lookup (emacs keymap) ──'
53	case "$key" in
54	  Ctrl+*)
55	    ksym=$(printf '^%s' "${key#Ctrl+}")
56	    bindkey -M emacs "$ksym" 2>/dev/null || echo '(not bound)'
57	    ;;
58	  Alt+*)
59	    rest=${key#Alt+}
60	    rest=$(printf '%s' "$rest" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
61	    ksym=$(printf '\\e%s' "$rest")
62	    bindkey -M emacs "$ksym" 2>/dev/null || echo '(not bound)'
63	    ;;
64	  Tab) bindkey -M emacs '^I' 2>/dev/null ;;
65	  End) bindkey -M emacs '^[[F' 2>/dev/null ;;
66	  *)   echo '(no live lookup)' ;;
67	esac
68	echo
69	echo '── Source files in ~/.config/zsh ──'
70	if [ -d "$HOME/.config/zsh" ]; then
71	    grep -rn "^${widget}()\\|zle -N ${widget}\\b" "$HOME/.config/zsh" 2>/dev/null | head -5
72	fi
73	"""
74	
75	[keybindings]

77	ctrl-y = "actions:copy"
78	
79	[actions.paste]

81	command = """

83	widget=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $2}')

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Source emitter for the `super-productivity` tv channel.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   super-productivity-source.sh <tasks-active|tasks-all|tasks-archived|projects|tags>
6	#
7	# Emits TSV rows: <id>\t<marker>\t<context>\t<title>
8	#
9	# Talks to Super Productivity's Local REST API on http://127.0.0.1:3876.
10	# Requires Super Productivity desktop ≥ 18.0.0 (the API was added in
11	# upstream PR #6981, first shipped in v18.0.0 on 2026-03-26). Older
12	# versions (e.g. 17.x) do not have the HTTP server at all — they will
13	# look "API down" no matter what setting you flip.
14	#
15	# To enable in v18+:
16	#   Settings → Misc → "Enable local REST API"
17	# (NOT in Sync & Export — that section only configures Dropbox/WebDAV/
18	# SuperSync data sync, which is unrelated to the REST API.)
19	#
20	# Reverse-engineered route reference: docs/tools/super-productivity.md
21	# Upstream source of truth (as of 2026-04):
22	#   electron/local-rest-api.ts
23	#   electron/shared-with-frontend/local-rest-api.model.ts
24	#   src/app/core/electron/local-rest-api-handler.service.ts
25	
26	set -u
27	
28	API="${SP_API_BASE:-http://127.0.0.1:3876}"
29	mode="${1:-tasks-active}"
30	
31	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	# Mode validation BEFORE preflight, so a typo doesn't get masked by API-down.
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	case "$mode" in
35	  tasks-active|tasks-all|tasks-archived|projects|tags) ;;
36	  *)
37	    printf '0\t⚠ unknown mode\t-\t%s (use tasks-active|tasks-all|tasks-archived|projects|tags)\n' "$mode" >&2
38	    exit 2
39	    ;;
40	esac
41	
42	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
43	# Preflight: GET /health is the one route that responds before the renderer
44	# is ready, so we use it as a liveness probe. -m 1 keeps `tv` snappy even
45	# when SP isn't running (TCP RST returns immediately on localhost; this
46	# 1s cap is for the rare case where the port is stuck).
47	#
48	# When the probe fails, we try to differentiate three cases by reading the
49	# installed app version from the macOS app bundle (Linux/other: skip detection
50	# and fall through to generic message):
51	#   1. SP not installed         → install hint
52	#   2. SP installed but < v18   → upgrade hint (REST API doesn't exist yet)
53	#   3. SP ≥ v18 + API down      → toggle hint (most common after upgrade)
54	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55	if ! curl -sf -m 1 "$API/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
56	  hint="Needs Super Productivity ≥ 18.0.0, then Settings → Misc → Enable Local REST API"
57	  if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ] && [ -f "/Applications/Super Productivity.app/Contents/Info.plist" ]; then
58	    sp_version=$(defaults read "/Applications/Super Productivity.app/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString 2>/dev/null || echo "")
59	    sp_major="${sp_version%%.*}"
60	    if [ -n "$sp_major" ] && [ "$sp_major" -ge 18 ] 2>/dev/null; then
61	      hint="SP $sp_version installed but API not responding — open SP, Settings → Misc → Enable Local REST API, then restart SP"
62	    elif [ -n "$sp_version" ]; then
63	      hint="SP $sp_version is too old for REST API — run: brew upgrade --cask super-productivity (need ≥ 18.0.0)"
64	    else
65	      hint="Super Productivity not installed — run: brew install --cask super-productivity"
66	    fi
67	  fi
68	  printf '0\t⚠ API down\tv18+\t%s\n' "$hint"
69	  exit 0
70	fi
71	
72	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	# Project-id → title cache (5s TTL). Tasks reference projects by id only,
74	# so without this we'd need a JOIN per row. One GET /projects per refresh
75	# cycle keeps the channel responsive.
76	#
77	# Response envelope: all routes return `{"ok": bool, "data": <payload>}`.
78	# We extract `.data` once at fetch time so downstream jq pipelines see the
79	# raw payload (array/object), not the wrapper.
80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	cache="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sp-projects-${UID:-$(id -u)}.json"
82	mtime() {
83	  if stat -f %m "$1" 2>/dev/null; then return; fi
84	  stat -c %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null
85	}
86	if [ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(($(date +%s) - $(mtime "$cache" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)))" -gt 5 ]; then
87	  curl -sf -m 2 "$API/projects" 2>/dev/null | jq '.data // []' >"$cache" 2>/dev/null \
88	    || echo '[]' >"$cache"
89	fi
90	
91	# Current task id (for the ▶ marker on the active row). Empty if no task is
92	# focused; the API returns {ok:true, data:null} when nothing is active.
93	current=$(curl -sf -m 2 "$API/task-control/current" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.data.id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
94	
95	emit_tasks() {
96	  # $1 = query string suffix (e.g. "source=active&includeDone=false")
97	  # $2 = marker style: "current" | "done" | "archived"
98	  local qs="$1" style="$2"
99	  curl -sf -m 3 "$API/tasks?$qs" 2>/dev/null \
100	    | jq -r --arg cur "$current" --arg style "$style" --slurpfile projs "$cache" '
101	        ($projs[0] | map({(.id): .title}) | add) as $pmap
102	        | .data[]
103	        | . as $t
104	        | (
105	            if   $style == "current"  then (if .id == $cur then "▶ active"
106	                                            else "○ pending" end)
107	            elif $style == "done"     then (if .isDone     then "✓ done"
108	                                            elif .id == $cur then "▶ active"
109	                                            else "○ pending" end)
110	            elif $style == "archived" then "📦 archived"
111	            else "○" end
112	          ) as $marker
113	        | ($pmap[.projectId] // "no-project") as $proj
114	        | [ .id, $marker, $proj, .title ] | @tsv'
115	}
116	
117	case "$mode" in
118	  tasks-active)
119	    emit_tasks "source=active&includeDone=false" "current"
120	    ;;
121	  tasks-all)
122	    emit_tasks "source=active&includeDone=true" "done"
123	    ;;
124	  tasks-archived)
125	    emit_tasks "source=archived&includeDone=true" "archived"
126	    ;;
127	  projects)
128	    curl -sf -m 3 "$API/projects" 2>/dev/null \
129	      | jq -r '.data[] | [
130	            .id,
131	            (if .isArchived then "📦 archived" else "○ active" end),
132	            ((.taskIds // [] | length | tostring) + " tasks"),
133	            .title
134	          ] | @tsv'
135	    ;;
136	  tags)
137	    curl -sf -m 3 "$API/tags" 2>/dev/null \
138	      | jq -r '.data[] | [
139	            .id,
140	            "🏷",
141	            (.color // "no-color"),
142	            .title
143	          ] | @tsv'
144	    ;;
145	esac
146
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Source emitter for the `clash` and `clash-api` tv channels.
3	# Usage:
4	#   clash-source.sh <proxies|groups|rules|summary|api>
5	#   clash-source.sh <api-proxies|api-groups|api-rules|api-groups-for-switch>
6	#
7	# YAML-backed modes emit rows from the resolved Clash config. Controller-backed
8	# modes talk to the live Clash / mihomo external-controller HTTP API.
9	
10	set -u
11	
12	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
13	PARSE="$SELF_DIR/clash-parse.py"
14	
15	mode="${1:-proxies}"
16	
17	ctrl_host=""
18	ctrl_secret=""
19	auth=()
20	base=""
21	
22	parse_available() {
23	  [ -x "$PARSE" ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1
24	}
25	
26	emit_parse_prereq_row() {
27	  if [ ! -x "$PARSE" ]; then
28	    printf 'none\tclash-parse-missing\t-\t%s is not executable\t-\n' "$PARSE"
29	  else
30	    printf 'none\tuv-not-installed\t-\tRun chezmoi bootstrap to install uv\t-\n'
31	  fi
32	}
33	
34	run_parse() {
35	  if ! parse_available; then
36	    emit_parse_prereq_row
37	    return 1
38	  fi
39	  "$PARSE" "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
40	}
41	
42	resolve_controller() {
43	  if [ -n "${CLASH_CONTROLLER:-}" ]; then
44	    printf '%s\n%s\n' "$CLASH_CONTROLLER" "${CLASH_SECRET:-}"
45	    return 0
46	  fi

Perfect! Now I have enough information. Let me write up the comprehensive findings:

## Television Channel Configuration Analysis

I've thoroughly explored the television (tv) channel configuration in your repo. Here's the complete pattern for designing an MLflow channel:

### 1. **General TOML Schema (Required & Optional Fields)**

Every channel follows this structure:

**Required sections:**
- `[metadata]` — name, description, optional requirements (tools needed)
- `[source]` — command(s) producing TSV/list output; display/output row format
- `[preview]` — command(s) for cycling preview views
- `[keybindings]` — optional custom key actions (defaults handled globally)
- `[actions.*]` — implementations of custom keybindings

**Key fields:**
- `command` — string or array (TSV output for source; plaintext/JSON for preview)
- `display` — how to format rows using `{split:\t:N}` or `{split:\<char>:N}` placeholders
- `output` — what gets emitted when Enter is pressed; also `{split:...}` syntax
- `watch` — seconds between auto-refresh (e.g., 2.0 for pueue, 5.0 for super-productivity)
- `no_sort` — true to prevent TV's default alphabetical sort
- `header` — preview title using placeholders

### 2. **Template Pattern (`.toml.tmpl` Files)**

Templates are used exclusively for **cross-platform conditionals** and **chezmoi data injection**:

- **`mac-procs.toml.tmpl`** — wrapped in `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}...{{ end -}}` (macOS only; Linux gets deleted)
- **`services.toml.tmpl`** — two complete source/action sets: one for Linux systemd, one for macOS launchd (same key names, different implementations)
- **`disk.toml.tmpl`**, **`users.toml.tmpl`**, **`scheduled-jobs.toml.tmpl`** — similar OS conditionals

**Not templated when:** channel is platform-agnostic (clash-api, pueue, super-productivity are all `.toml`).

For MLflow: use `.toml` unless your channel needs OS-specific behavior.

### 3. **Placeholder Syntax for Selected Items**

TV uses **field splitting + indexing**:
- `{split:\t:0}` — first field (source command splits on tab by default)
- `{split:\t:2}` — third field
- `{split: :0}` — first space-separated field (used in mac-procs for PID extraction)
- `{split:\\t:0}` — escaped in triple-quoted strings (prevents TOML parser from eating backslash)
- `{strip_ansi}` — remove ANSI color codes

**Important:** The comment in agent-sessions.toml warns: *"do NOT embed Python/awk/JSON literals inline here — any bare `{...}` (outside TV's own placeholders) silently breaks ALL placeholder substitution."*

### 4. **Runtime Configuration (Env Vars vs Hardcoding)**

**Existing patterns:**

- **`clash-api.toml`** — reads `$CLASH_CONTROLLER` and `$CLASH_SECRET` env vars, then delegates controller discovery to a helper script (`clash-source.sh`), which tries: explicit env → parsed YAML config (via `clash-parse.py`) → localhost 127.0.0.1:9090 as fallback.

- **`super-productivity.toml`** — hardcoded to `http://127.0.0.1:3876` (no env var override currently; the source helper reads it from the app's settings if needed). Note at top of the file says "requires desktop Electron app with Local REST API enabled."

**Recommendation for MLflow:** Follow clash-api pattern:
```bash
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-http://127.0.0.1:5000}"
```
This allows users to override at runtime while providing a sensible localhost default.

### 5. **Existing HTTP API Channels**

**`clash-api.toml`** (most relevant):
- Uses helper scripts: `clash-source.sh`, `clash-preview.sh`, `clash-parse.py`
- Source emits: kind (proxy/group/rule), name, metadata — TSV columns
- Preview cycles: JSON detail → latency probe → meta relationships
- Actions: `test_latency` (calls `/delay`), `switch_proxy`, `close_connections` (DELETE /connections), `reload_config` (PUT with JSON body)
- Requirements: curl, uv (for YAML parsing)

**`super-productivity.toml`** (simpler, best mimic):
- Direct `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/{id}` in preview command
- Source helper (shell script) handles preflight health check, caching, mode routing
- Output: TSV with id, marker (▶/✓/○), project, title
- Actions: open-detail (jq pretty), copy-id, copy-title, dump-json
- Requirements: curl, jq

**`pueue.toml`** (JSON-heavy):
- Source pipes `pueue status --json` to jq for filtering
- Two action hooks: `reload_source` (implicit `ctrl-r`) after mutations to refresh
- Demonstrates keybinding chains: `alt-p = ["actions:pause", "reload_source"]`

### 6. **Cleanest Example to Mimic: `super-productivity.toml`**

```toml
[metadata]
name = "super-productivity"
description = "Super Productivity (read-only): browse tasks, projects, tags via local REST API"
requirements = ["curl", "jq"]

[source]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-active",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-all",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tasks-archived",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh projects",
  "~/.config/television/super-productivity-source.sh tags",
]
display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:1}  [{split:\t:2}]  {split:\t:3}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"
watch = 5.0
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data || echo 'No JSON detail for this row (project/tag entries do not have a /tasks/:id endpoint, or API is unreachable).'",
  "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.data.notes // \"(no notes)\"' || echo '(no notes available)'",
]
header = "{split:\t:1}  {split:\t:3}"

[ui]
input_header = "Super Productivity"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open-detail"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
alt-y = "actions:copy-title"

[actions.open-detail]
description = "Open full JSON detail in pager"
command = "curl -sf -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:3876/tasks/'{split:\t:0}' 2>/dev/null | jq -C .data | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-id]
description = "Copy row id to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"
```

**Why this is cleanest:**
- No `.tmpl` (platform-agnostic)
- Helper script handles health checks + error messaging (keeps TOML lean)
- Source cycles via array of commands (Ctrl+S toggles)
- Preview cycles via array too (Ctrl+F)
- Actions clearly separated (`mode: "execute"` for interactive, `mode: "fork"` for async)
- Requirements declared upfront
- Tab-delimited TSV (simpler than jq pipes in source)
