1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Source emitter for the `super-productivity` tv channel.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   super-productivity-source.sh <tasks-active|tasks-all|tasks-archived|projects|tags>
6	#
7	# Emits TSV rows: <id>\t<marker>\t<context>\t<title>
8	#
9	# Talks to Super Productivity's Local REST API on http://127.0.0.1:3876.
10	# Requires Super Productivity desktop ≥ 18.0.0 (the API was added in
11	# upstream PR #6981, first shipped in v18.0.0 on 2026-03-26). Older
12	# versions (e.g. 17.x) do not have the HTTP server at all — they will
13	# look "API down" no matter what setting you flip.
14	#
15	# To enable in v18+:
16	#   Settings → Misc → "Enable local REST API"
17	# (NOT in Sync & Export — that section only configures Dropbox/WebDAV/
18	# SuperSync data sync, which is unrelated to the REST API.)
19	#
20	# Reverse-engineered route reference: docs/tools/super-productivity.md
21	# Upstream source of truth (as of 2026-04):
22	#   electron/local-rest-api.ts
23	#   electron/shared-with-frontend/local-rest-api.model.ts
24	#   src/app/core/electron/local-rest-api-handler.service.ts
25	
26	set -u
27	
28	API="${SP_API_BASE:-http://127.0.0.1:3876}"
29	mode="${1:-tasks-active}"
30	
31	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	# Mode validation BEFORE preflight, so a typo doesn't get masked by API-down.
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	case "$mode" in
35	  tasks-active|tasks-all|tasks-archived|projects|tags) ;;
36	  *)
37	    printf '0\t⚠ unknown mode\t-\t%s (use tasks-active|tasks-all|tasks-archived|projects|tags)\n' "$mode" >&2
38	    exit 2
39	    ;;
40	esac
41	
42	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
43	# Preflight: GET /health is the one route that responds before the renderer
44	# is ready, so we use it as a liveness probe. -m 1 keeps `tv` snappy even
45	# when SP isn't running (TCP RST returns immediately on localhost; this
46	# 1s cap is for the rare case where the port is stuck).
47	#
48	# When the probe fails, we try to differentiate three cases by reading the
49	# installed app version from the macOS app bundle (Linux/other: skip detection
50	# and fall through to generic message):
51	#   1. SP not installed         → install hint
52	#   2. SP installed but < v18   → upgrade hint (REST API doesn't exist yet)
53	#   3. SP ≥ v18 + API down      → toggle hint (most common after upgrade)
54	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55	if ! curl -sf -m 1 "$API/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
56	  hint="Needs Super Productivity ≥ 18.0.0, then Settings → Misc → Enable Local REST API"
57	  if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ] && [ -f "/Applications/Super Productivity.app/Contents/Info.plist" ]; then
58	    sp_version=$(defaults read "/Applications/Super Productivity.app/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString 2>/dev/null || echo "")
59	    sp_major="${sp_version%%.*}"
60	    if [ -n "$sp_major" ] && [ "$sp_major" -ge 18 ] 2>/dev/null; then
61	      hint="SP $sp_version installed but API not responding — open SP, Settings → Misc → Enable Local REST API, then restart SP"
62	    elif [ -n "$sp_version" ]; then
63	      hint="SP $sp_version is too old for REST API — run: brew upgrade --cask super-productivity (need ≥ 18.0.0)"
64	    else
65	      hint="Super Productivity not installed — run: brew install --cask super-productivity"
66	    fi
67	  fi
68	  printf '0\t⚠ API down\tv18+\t%s\n' "$hint"
69	  exit 0
70	fi
71	
72	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	# Project-id → title cache (5s TTL). Tasks reference projects by id only,
74	# so without this we'd need a JOIN per row. One GET /projects per refresh
75	# cycle keeps the channel responsive.
76	#
77	# Response envelope: all routes return `{"ok": bool, "data": <payload>}`.
78	# We extract `.data` once at fetch time so downstream jq pipelines see the
79	# raw payload (array/object), not the wrapper.
80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	cache="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sp-projects-${UID:-$(id -u)}.json"
82	mtime() {
83	  if stat -f %m "$1" 2>/dev/null; then return; fi
84	  stat -c %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null
85	}
86	if [ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(($(date +%s) - $(mtime "$cache" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)))" -gt 5 ]; then
87	  curl -sf -m 2 "$API/projects" 2>/dev/null | jq '.data // []' >"$cache" 2>/dev/null \
88	    || echo '[]' >"$cache"
89	fi
90	
91	# Current task id (for the ▶ marker on the active row). Empty if no task is
92	# focused; the API returns {ok:true, data:null} when nothing is active.
93	current=$(curl -sf -m 2 "$API/task-control/current" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.data.id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
94	
95	emit_tasks() {
96	  # $1 = query string suffix (e.g. "source=active&includeDone=false")
97	  # $2 = marker style: "current" | "done" | "archived"
98	  local qs="$1" style="$2"
99	  curl -sf -m 3 "$API/tasks?$qs" 2>/dev/null \
100	    | jq -r --arg cur "$current" --arg style "$style" --slurpfile projs "$cache" '
101	        ($projs[0] | map({(.id): .title}) | add) as $pmap
102	        | .data[]
103	        | . as $t
104	        | (
105	            if   $style == "current"  then (if .id == $cur then "▶ active"
106	                                            else "○ pending" end)
107	            elif $style == "done"     then (if .isDone     then "✓ done"
108	                                            elif .id == $cur then "▶ active"
109	                                            else "○ pending" end)
110	            elif $style == "archived" then "📦 archived"
111	            else "○" end
112	          ) as $marker
113	        | ($pmap[.projectId] // "no-project") as $proj
114	        | [ .id, $marker, $proj, .title ] | @tsv'
115	}
116	
117	case "$mode" in
118	  tasks-active)
119	    emit_tasks "source=active&includeDone=false" "current"
120	    ;;
121	  tasks-all)
122	    emit_tasks "source=active&includeDone=true" "done"
123	    ;;
124	  tasks-archived)
125	    emit_tasks "source=archived&includeDone=true" "archived"
126	    ;;
127	  projects)
128	    curl -sf -m 3 "$API/projects" 2>/dev/null \
129	      | jq -r '.data[] | [
130	            .id,
131	            (if .isArchived then "📦 archived" else "○ active" end),
132	            ((.taskIds // [] | length | tostring) + " tasks"),
133	            .title
134	          ] | @tsv'
135	    ;;
136	  tags)
137	    curl -sf -m 3 "$API/tags" 2>/dev/null \
138	      | jq -r '.data[] | [
139	            .id,
140	            "🏷",
141	            (.color // "no-color"),
142	            .title
143	          ] | @tsv'
144	    ;;
145	esac
146
```

**Which backend strategy should the helper use?**

Options:
- **Pure Python (mlflow API)** - Single code path. Works for file/sqlite/http uniformly. Pays ~1-2s mlflow import cost per invocation.
- **Hybrid: REST when http://, Python fallback** - Faster on the LAN server (curl+jq, no Python import). Two code paths to maintain. Falls back to Python for file/sqlite URIs.
- **REST API only** - Fastest but cannot read file:./mlruns or sqlite:///mlflow.db — would skip 2 of the 3 modes you explicitly mentioned.

**Which entity views should v1 include?** _(select multiple)_

Options:
- **Experiments** - List all active experiments (id, name, last_update, artifact_location).
- **Recent runs (flat)** - Top N runs across ALL experiments sorted by start_time desc. Includes experiment_name column so you can fuzzy-search to filter.
- **Registered models** - Models in the Model Registry (name, latest_versions, stage). Optional — registry isn't always used.
- **Runs scoped to an experiment** - Drill-down via a pinning env var (e.g. MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID) or a TV action that re-launches the channel with the experiment fixed.

**Where should the channel + helper script live?**

Options:
- **dot_config/television/ alongside other channels** - Same dir as super-productivity-source.sh / clash-source.sh. Independent feature. Auto-deploys on chezmoi apply.
- **Bundled into the mlflow-tracking skill** - Put the helper script under .claude/skills/mlflow-tracking/scripts/ and have the TV channel call it from there. Tighter coupling to the skill docs.

**Should MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI be configurable per-channel-launch?**

Options:
- **Just read env var (set it before `tv mlflow`)** - Simplest. User runs `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow`. Default falls through to mlflow's own (`file:./mlruns` in CWD).
- **Env var + shell alias for the LAN server** - Plus a convenience alias like `tv-mlflow-lan` that sets URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 before launching. Keeps localhost/file modes default and gives one-keystroke access to the shared server.
- **Source cycle includes URI presets** - Cycle through env-defined presets (LAN server / localhost / ./mlruns) as separate source commands. More complex but lets you switch backends without leaving TV.

```md
# Add an MLflow Television (tv) channel

## Context

The user runs experiments against three MLflow backends — local `./mlruns` files, a local `sqlite:///mlflow.db`, and a LAN server at `http://192.168.222.207:15002/`. There is no current way to fuzzy-search experiments or runs from the terminal: the MLflow web UI is one tab, and `mlflow runs list` only emits a Rich-formatted text table (no JSON). The `mlflow` CLI is already installed via `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml:49` and the `mlflow-tracking` agent skill documents the three deployment modes, so the missing piece is an interactive picker.

We will add a `tv mlflow` channel that lists experiments / recent runs / experiment-scoped runs / registered models, previews each entity as JSON, and supports copying IDs and opening them in the browser when the tracking URI is HTTP. The helper is a single Python script using `mlflow.MlflowClient`, because it is the only backend strategy that handles file, sqlite, and HTTP URIs uniformly (REST API alone would skip 2 of 3 modes; CLI list output is not JSON).

## Approach

### Design decisions

- **Pure Python helper.** One `MlflowClient` against `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (env-var-only, no aliases / no source-cycling presets). When the URI is unset, MLflow's own default (`file:./mlruns` in CWD) is used.
- **Helper layout = same as `super-productivity-source.sh`.** Channel TOML stays lean; helper handles preflight, hint rows on failure, and TSV emission. Cycles via separate source commands (Ctrl+S inside TV).
- **No `watch =`.** mlflow imports cost ~1–2s (pydantic + sqlalchemy); auto-refresh would be sluggish. Manual `Ctrl+R` reload is fine — experiments/runs change on the minute scale, not seconds.
- **Pydantic deprecation noise is suppressed** in the helper via `PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore` env + `warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)` so stderr doesn't leak into source rows.
- **Drill-down via env var, not nested actions.** `runs-experiment` source reads `$MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID`; if unset, it emits a single hint row pointing at the env var. An `alt-r` action re-execs `tv mlflow` with the highlighted experiment's id exported, giving a one-keystroke drill-down without state plumbing.

### Files to create

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml` | Channel definition — 4 source modes, 2 preview modes, 5 keybindings/actions |
| `dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-source.py` | TSV emitter for source modes; preflight + hint-row on failure |
| `dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-preview.py` | JSON detail / metrics summary for preview |

Both helpers use `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` with PEP 723 inline deps pinning `mlflow>=3.4` (the version already installed). This keeps them invokable on any host where `uv` is present, even outside the `mlflow` uv tool's site-packages — consistent with how `executable_clash-parse.py` is structured (it's a `uv run --script` file too).

### Helper script behavior

`mlflow-source.py <mode>` where `<mode>` ∈ `experiments | runs-recent | runs-experiment | models`:

1. `os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONWARNINGS", "ignore")` + `warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")`.
2. Resolve `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`; if set, `mlflow.set_tracking_uri(...)`.
3. Preflight: `MlflowClient().search_experiments(max_results=1)`. On any exception emit one hint row:
   `0\t⚠ unreachable\t<scheme>\tCheck MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=<uri> — <short err msg>` and exit 0.
4. Emit TSV per mode:
   - `experiments` → `<exp_id>\t📊\t<lifecycle>\t<name>\t<last_update_iso>`
   - `runs-recent` → `<run_id>\t<status_icon>\t<exp_name>\t<run_name|short_id>\t<start_iso>` (top 50 by `start_time` desc, across all experiments)
   - `runs-experiment` → same shape as `runs-recent` but filtered to `$MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID`; hint row if env var unset
   - `models` → `<model_name>\t📦\t<latest_version_stage>\t<description_first_line>\t<last_updated_iso>`
5. Status icon mapping: `RUNNING`→`▶`, `FINISHED`→`✓`, `FAILED`→`✗`, `KILLED`→`■`, `SCHEDULED`→`○`.

`mlflow-preview.py <kind> <id>` where `<kind>` ∈ `experiment | run | model`:

- For `run`: pretty-print `client.get_run(run_id)` as JSON (params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, status, timestamps). Two views via TV preview-cycle: full JSON, or metrics-only summary (last value per metric key).
- For `experiment`: pretty-print `client.get_experiment(exp_id)` + a short tail of its 5 most recent runs.
- For `model`: pretty-print `client.get_registered_model(name)` with latest versions.

Hint row case (`id == "0"`): preview emits `Help: set MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://... or sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, then Ctrl+R to reload.`

### Channel TOML structure

Mirror `dot_config/television/cable/super-productivity.toml:57-118` exactly — same `[metadata]`, `[source]` (array of commands → Ctrl+S cycles), `[preview]` (array → Ctrl+F cycles), `[ui.preview_panel].size = 60`, `[keybindings]`, and per-action `[actions.*]` tables.

Source array (cycles in this order):

\```
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models
\```

Preview array (cycles in this order):

\```
~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\t:0}' --view full
~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\t:0}' --view metrics
\```

`auto` lets the preview script infer entity kind from id shape (uuid-like → run, integer → experiment, otherwise → model) — simpler than threading the source mode through.

Keybindings:

| Key | Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Enter` | `open-detail` | Full JSON in `less -R`, then "press Enter to exit" |
| `Ctrl+Y` | `copy-id` | Overrides TV's default (which copies the whole display row) |
| `Ctrl+O` | `open-browser` | No-op + message if URI is not `http(s)://` |
| `Alt+R` | `drill-runs` | Re-exec `MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID=<id> tv mlflow` (only meaningful on experiment rows) |
| `Alt+J` | `dump-json` | Print JSON to terminal, paged |

`requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]` in `[metadata]`. `uv` because the helpers are `uv run --script`; `mlflow` because that's the import target. `jq` is NOT a hard requirement — the Python helper does its own JSON formatting via `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` and colorizes with `rich` if available, plain otherwise.

### Reuse from the existing codebase

- Clipboard helper pattern: lift the `_clip` shell function verbatim from `dot_config/television/cable/super-productivity.toml:107` (pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC52 fallback chain). Already battle-tested across mac/Linux/SSH.
- Preflight / hint-row pattern: same shape as `executable_super-productivity-source.sh:55-70` — single row with id `0`, emoji marker, actionable hint.
- `uv run --script` shebang + PEP 723 frontmatter: see `executable_clash-parse.py` for the convention used in this repo.

### Files to modify

- `.claude/skills/mlflow-tracking/SKILL.md` — append a short "Browse from terminal: `tv mlflow`" pointer near the deployment-modes section. Optional, low priority.

### Files NOT touched (and why)

- `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` — `mlflow` is already pinned (no version bump needed).
- `CLAUDE.md` cross-file table — no MkDocs doc surface created, no new chezmoi prompt, no new shell alias / function, no new keybinding under `Ctrl+`/`Alt+` in the *shell* config (`Alt+R` is scoped to the TV channel context, which falls outside the `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` aliases / `docs/shells/keybindings.md` tables).
- `docs/shells/aliases.md` — no shell alias added (user opted against an alias).
- `README.md` — channel addition is not a new platform / role / setup step.

## Verification

1. **Schema lint** — open `mlflow.toml` in any TOML linter; ensure `{split:\\t:N}` placeholders survive (triple-quoted strings only where backslashes need it).
2. **Local file mode** —
   \```
   cd /tmp && mkdir -p mlrun-test && cd mlrun-test
   uv run python -c "import mlflow; mlflow.set_experiment('demo'); mlflow.start_run(); mlflow.log_param('x', 1); mlflow.end_run()"
   tv mlflow
   \```
   Expect: `demo` experiment listed under Ctrl+S source 1; one run under source 2.
3. **SQLite mode** —
   \```
   cd /tmp/mlrun-test && MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
   \```
   Expect: empty list (fresh sqlite) → log one run → Ctrl+R → reappears.
4. **LAN HTTP server** —
   \```
   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
   \```
   Expect: real experiments from the user's earlier curl smoke (`Dev/PlainTextProgress_Test`, `WF_Proxy_Test`, …) under source 1. Ctrl+F should cycle full-JSON ↔ metrics-only previews. Ctrl+O should open the run/experiment in the system browser.
5. **Failure-path UI** —
   \```
   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://no-such-host:9999 tv mlflow
   \```
   Expect: single yellow hint row, no crash, no Python traceback leaking into the source view.
6. **Drill-down** — highlight an experiment row → `Alt+R` → TV re-launches scoped to that experiment → source 3 (`runs-experiment`) now shows real rows. Exit TV → original env restored.
7. **`tv channels`** lists the new entry with description.
8. **App-level validation** (per repo invariant "Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax") — `tv --version >/dev/null && tv mlflow --help 2>&1` to confirm TV parses the TOML cleanly; no error from the cable loader.

`mlflow-source.py <mode>` where `<mode>` ∈ `experiments | runs-recent | runs-experiment | models`:

1. `os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONWARNINGS", "ignore")` + `warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")`.
2. Resolve `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`; if set, `mlflow.set_tracking_uri(...)`.
3. Preflight: `MlflowClient().search_experiments(max_results=1)`. On any exception emit one hint row:
   `0\t⚠ unreachable\t<scheme>\tCheck MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=<uri> — <short err msg>` and exit 0.
4. Emit TSV per mode:
   - `experiments` → `<exp_id>\t📊\t<lifecycle>\t<name>\t<last_update_iso>`
   - `runs-recent` → `<run_id>\t<status_icon>\t<exp_name>\t<run_name|short_id>\t<start_iso>` (top 50 by `start_time` desc, across all experiments)
   - `runs-experiment` → same shape as `runs-recent` but filtered to `$MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID`; hint row if env var unset
   - `models` → `<model_name>\t📦\t<latest_version_stage>\t<description_first_line>\t<last_updated_iso>`
5. Status icon mapping: `RUNNING`→`▶`, `FINISHED`→`✓`, `FAILED`→`✗`, `KILLED`→`■`, `SCHEDULED`→`○`.

`mlflow-preview.py <kind> <id>` where `<kind>` ∈ `experiment | run | model`:

- For `run`: pretty-print `client.get_run(run_id)` as JSON (params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, status, timestamps). Two views via TV preview-cycle: full JSON, or metrics-only summary (last value per metric key).
- For `experiment`: pretty-print `client.get_experiment(exp_id)` + a short tail of its 5 most recent runs.
- For `model`: pretty-print `client.get_registered_model(name)` with latest versions.

Hint row case (`id == "0"`): preview emits `Help: set MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://... or sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, then Ctrl+R to reload.`

### Channel TOML structure

Mirror `dot_config/television/cable/super-productivity.toml:57-118` exactly — same `[metadata]`, `[source]` (array of commands → Ctrl+S cycles), `[preview]` (array → Ctrl+F cycles), `[ui.preview_panel].size = 60`, `[keybindings]`, and per-action `[actions.*]` tables.

Source array (cycles in this order):

```
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment
~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models
```

Preview array (cycles in this order):

```
~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\t:0}' --view full
~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\t:0}' --view metrics
```

`auto` lets the preview script infer entity kind from id shape (uuid-like → run, integer → experiment, otherwise → model) — simpler than threading the source mode through.

Keybindings:

| Key | Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Enter` | `open-detail` | Full JSON in `less -R`, then "press Enter to exit" |
| `Ctrl+Y` | `copy-id` | Overrides TV's default (which copies the whole display row) |
| `Ctrl+O` | `open-browser` | No-op + message if URI is not `http(s)://` |
| `Alt+R` | `drill-runs` | Re-exec `MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID=<id> tv mlflow` (only meaningful on experiment rows) |
| `Alt+J` | `dump-json` | Print JSON to terminal, paged |

`requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]` in `[metadata]`. `uv` because the helpers are `uv run --script`; `mlflow` because that's the import target. `jq` is NOT a hard requirement — the Python helper does its own JSON formatting via `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` and colorizes with `rich` if available, plain otherwise.

### Reuse from the existing codebase

- Clipboard helper pattern: lift the `_clip` shell function verbatim from `dot_config/television/cable/super-productivity.toml:107` (pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC52 fallback chain). Already battle-tested across mac/Linux/SSH.
- Preflight / hint-row pattern: same shape as `executable_super-productivity-source.sh:55-70` — single row with id `0`, emoji marker, actionable hint.
- `uv run --script` shebang + PEP 723 frontmatter: see `executable_clash-parse.py` for the convention used in this repo.

### Files to modify

- `.claude/skills/mlflow-tracking/SKILL.md` — append a short "Browse from terminal: `tv mlflow`" pointer near the deployment-modes section. Optional, low priority.

### Files NOT touched (and why)

- `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` — `mlflow` is already pinned (no version bump needed).
- `CLAUDE.md` cross-file table — no MkDocs doc surface created, no new chezmoi prompt, no new shell alias / function, no new keybinding under `Ctrl+`/`Alt+` in the *shell* config (`Alt+R` is scoped to the TV channel context, which falls outside the `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` aliases / `docs/shells/keybindings.md` tables).
- `docs/shells/aliases.md` — no shell alias added (user opted against an alias).
- `README.md` — channel addition is not a new platform / role / setup step.

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = ["PyYAML>=6.0"]
5	# ///
6	"""Parser for Clash / mihomo config YAML files, used by the `clash` tv channel.
7	
8	Subcommands emit TSV rows for the TV source (`proxies`, `groups`, `rules`,
9	`summary`) or plain text for previews / copy actions (`path`, `yaml`, `server`,
10	`controller`).
11	
12	TSV schema: kind \t name \t type_or_meta \t server_or_target \t extra
13	kind ∈ {proxy, group, rule, config, none}
14	
15	Config discovery order (first existing file wins):
16	    $CLASH_CONFIG env var (explicit override)
17	    ~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml -> active profiles/<time>.yml
18	    ~/.config/clash/config.{yaml,yml}
19	    ~/.config/mihomo/config.{yaml,yml}
20	    ~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.{yaml,yml}   (macOS)
21	    ~/Library/Application Support/mihomo/config.{yaml,yml}  (macOS)
22	
23	Parsed config is cached as YAML.safe_load output; this script never writes back
24	to the config file.
25	"""
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import os
30	import sys
31	from pathlib import Path
32	
33	import yaml
34	
35	
36	def _runtime_candidate_paths() -> list[Path]:
37	    home = Path.home()
38	    paths: list[Path] = []
39	    for base in (
40	        home / ".config" / "clash",
41	        home / ".config" / "mihomo",
42	        home / "Library" / "Application Support" / "clash",
43	        home / "Library" / "Application Support" / "mihomo",
44	        ):
45	        for ext in ("config.yaml", "config.yml"):
46	            paths.append(base / ext)
47	    return paths
48	
49	
50	def _active_profile_path() -> Path | None:
51	    list_path = Path.home() / ".config" / "clash" / "profiles" / "list.yml"
52	    try:
53	        if not list_path.is_file():
54	            return None
55	    except OSError:
56	        return None
57	
58	    try:
59	        with list_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
60	            data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
61	    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError):
62	        return None
63	
64	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
65	        return None
66	
67	    files = data.get("files")
68	    index = data.get("index")
69	    if not isinstance(files, list) or not isinstance(index, int) or not (0 <= index < len(files)):
70	        return None
71	
72	    entry = files[index]
73	    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
74	        return None
75	
76	    raw_name = entry.get("time") or entry.get("file") or entry.get("path")
77	    if raw_name is None:
78	        return None
79	
80	    raw_name = str(raw_name).strip()
81	    if not raw_name:
82	        return None
83	
84	    candidate = Path(raw_name).expanduser()
85	    if candidate.is_absolute():
86	        return candidate if candidate.is_file() else None
87	
88	    base = list_path.parent
89	    variants = [base / raw_name]
90	    if candidate.suffix not in {".yml", ".yaml"}:
91	        variants.extend((base / f"{raw_name}.yml", base / f"{raw_name}.yaml"))

93	    for variant in variants:
94	        try:

97	        except OSError:

99	    return None

122	    """Return (path, error_detail).

124	    When $CLASH_CONFIG is set we treat it as an explicit override — if the path

126	    common paths (picking up the wrong config and leaking credentials in

138	    for p in _default_candidate_paths():

153	def _clean(value: object) -> str:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unified agent-session enumerator for the `agent-sessions` tv channel.

Walks session storage for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor and emits
a single TSV stream with stable columns:

  0. agent tag        ([oc] / [cc] / [cx] / [cu] / [ci])
  1. when             (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, local time)
  2. session id       (full id; passed to <agent> --resume / --session)
  3. directory        (absolute cwd; "?" when unknown)
  4. title/snippet    (first non-system user message, truncated)
  5. specstory_path   (matching .specstory/history/*.md file, or empty)

In `all` mode rows from every agent are collected into one buffer, sorted
globally by raw mtime DESC, and then printed — otherwise TV sees each
agent's block sorted internally but concatenated, which looks random.

Usage (called from cable/agent-sessions.toml):

  agent-sessions.py all       # all five agents merged, globally sorted
  agent-sessions.py opencode  # opencode-only
  agent-sessions.py claude    # claude-only
  agent-sessions.py codex     # codex-only
  agent-sessions.py cursor    # cursor Agent CLI only
  agent-sessions.py cursor-ide                # Cursor IDE composer chats only
  agent-sessions.py transcript <cc|cx|oc> <sid>  # render full back-and-forth
                                                 # as markdown on stdout.

Column 5 (specstory_path) is produced by grep'ing each file under
$SPECSTORY_HISTORY_DIRS (default: ~/.local/share/chezmoi/.specstory/history)
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = ["mlflow>=3.4"]
# ///
"""Source emitter for the `mlflow` tv channel.

Usage:
    mlflow-source.py <experiments|runs-recent|runs-experiment|models>

Emits TSV rows. Column 0 is always the id that TV passes to the preview
command (experiment_id / run_id / model_name). Column 1 is an emoji or
status marker; remaining columns are display-only.

Backend resolution honours `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (env var). When unset,
mlflow falls back to `file:./mlruns` in the current directory.

On any unreachable / unconfigured backend, a single hint row with id `0`
is emitted instead of crashing — preserves the same UX as the
super-productivity channel.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import warnings
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Iterable

os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONWARNINGS", "ignore")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import mlflow  # noqa: E402
from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient  # noqa: E402

MAX_EXPERIMENTS = 200
MAX_RUNS = 50

STATUS_ICON = {
    "RUNNING": "▶ running",
    "FINISHED": "✓ done",
    "FAILED": "✗ failed",
    "KILLED": "■ killed",
    "SCHEDULED": "○ scheduled",
}


def _clean(value: object) -> str:
    s = "" if value is None else str(value)
    return s.replace("\t", " ").replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", " ")


def tsv(*cols: object) -> None:
    print("\t".join(_clean(c) for c in cols))


def _ms_to_iso(ms: int | None) -> str:
    if not ms:
        return "-"
    try:
        dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ms) / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).astimezone()
        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
    except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError):
        return "-"


def _hint(reason: str, detail: str) -> None:
    uri = mlflow.get_tracking_uri() or "(unset)"
    tsv("0", f"⚠ {reason}", uri[:48], detail)


def _list_experiments(client: MlflowClient) -> list:
    return list(client.search_experiments(max_results=MAX_EXPERIMENTS))


def cmd_experiments(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
    exps = _list_experiments(client)
    if not exps:
        tsv("0", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No experiments — log a run to see it here")
        return
    for e in exps:
        tsv(
            e.experiment_id,
            "📊",
            e.lifecycle_stage or "-",
            e.name or "(unnamed)",
            _ms_to_iso(e.last_update_time),
        )


def _emit_runs(runs: Iterable, exp_name_by_id: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    count = 0
    for r in runs:
        info = r.info
        rid = info.run_id
        status = STATUS_ICON.get(info.status, info.status or "?")
        exp_name = exp_name_by_id.get(info.experiment_id, info.experiment_id)
        name = info.run_name or rid[:8]
        tsv(rid, status, exp_name, name, _ms_to_iso(info.start_time))
        count += 1
    return count


def cmd_runs_recent(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
    exps = _list_experiments(client)
    if not exps:
        tsv("0", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No experiments — log a run to see it here")
        return
    name_by_id = {e.experiment_id: (e.name or "(unnamed)") for e in exps}
    runs = client.search_runs(
        experiment_ids=list(name_by_id.keys()),
        max_results=MAX_RUNS,
        order_by=["attributes.start_time DESC"],
    )
    if _emit_runs(runs, name_by_id) == 0:
        tsv("0", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No runs yet — start a run to see it here")


def cmd_runs_experiment(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
    exp_id = os.environ.get("MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID", "").strip()
    if not exp_id:
        tsv(
            "0",
            "ℹ unscoped",
            "MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID",
            "Press Alt+R on an experiment row, or export MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID=<id> and Ctrl+R",
        )
        return
    try:
        exp = client.get_experiment(exp_id)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        _hint("not found", f"experiment_id={exp_id} — {str(e)[:80]}")
        return
    name_by_id = {exp.experiment_id: (exp.name or "(unnamed)")}
    runs = client.search_runs(
        experiment_ids=[exp.experiment_id],
        max_results=MAX_RUNS,
        order_by=["attributes.start_time DESC"],
    )
    if _emit_runs(runs, name_by_id) == 0:
        tsv("0", "ℹ empty", f"exp {exp.experiment_id}", f"No runs in '{exp.name}'")


def cmd_models(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
    try:
        models = list(client.search_registered_models(max_results=200))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        # Model registry isn't supported by file: backend at all.
        _hint("no registry", str(e)[:80])
        return
    if not models:
        tsv("0", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No registered models")
        return
    for m in models:
        stages = sorted({v.current_stage for v in (m.latest_versions or []) if v.current_stage})
        stage_label = ",".join(stages) if stages else "-"
        desc = (m.description or "").splitlines()[0] if m.description else ""
        tsv(
            m.name,
            "📦",
            stage_label,
            desc or "(no description)",
            _ms_to_iso(m.last_updated_timestamp),
        )


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2 or sys.argv[1] not in {
        "experiments",
        "runs-recent",
        "runs-experiment",
        "models",
    }:
        print(
            "usage: mlflow-source.py <experiments|runs-recent|runs-experiment|models>",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    mode = sys.argv[1]
    client = MlflowClient()

    # Preflight: any list call against the configured backend. Catches both
    # unreachable HTTP servers and unreadable file/sqlite paths.
    try:
        client.search_experiments(max_results=1)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        _hint("unreachable", str(e).splitlines()[0][:100])
        return 0

    if mode == "experiments":
        cmd_experiments(client)
    elif mode == "runs-recent":
        cmd_runs_recent(client)
    elif mode == "runs-experiment":
        cmd_runs_experiment(client)
    elif mode == "models":
        cmd_models(client)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = ["mlflow>=3.4"]
# ///
"""Preview emitter for the `mlflow` tv channel.

Usage:
    mlflow-preview.py auto <id> [--view full|metrics]

The `auto` kind inspects the id shape and routes to the right entity:
    - 32-hex-char id  -> run
    - all-digit id    -> experiment
    - anything else   -> registered model name

Output is human-readable JSON-ish. Uses rich's syntax highlighting when
present (mlflow itself depends on rich, so within the uv venv created by
the PEP 723 shebang above, rich is always available).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import warnings
from datetime import datetime, timezone

os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONWARNINGS", "ignore")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import mlflow  # noqa: E402
from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient  # noqa: E402

RUN_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{32}$")


def _ms_to_iso(ms: int | None) -> str:
    if not ms:
        return "-"
    try:
        dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ms) / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).astimezone()
        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z")
    except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError):
        return "-"


def _detect_kind(ident: str) -> str:
    if RUN_ID_RE.match(ident):
        return "run"
    if ident.isdigit():
        return "experiment"
    return "model"


def _emit(payload: dict | str) -> None:
    if isinstance(payload, str):
        print(payload)
        return
    try:
        from rich.console import Console
        Console(force_terminal=True, color_system="truecolor").print_json(
            json.dumps(payload, default=str)
        )
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str))


def _run_full(client: MlflowClient, run_id: str) -> dict:
    r = client.get_run(run_id)
    info = r.info
    data = r.data
    return {
        "run_id": info.run_id,
        "run_name": info.run_name,
        "experiment_id": info.experiment_id,
        "status": info.status,
        "start_time": _ms_to_iso(info.start_time),
        "end_time": _ms_to_iso(info.end_time),
        "user_id": info.user_id,
        "artifact_uri": info.artifact_uri,
        "lifecycle_stage": info.lifecycle_stage,
        "params": dict(data.params or {}),
        "metrics": dict(data.metrics or {}),
        "tags": {k: v for k, v in (data.tags or {}).items() if not k.startswith("mlflow.")},
        "mlflow_tags": {k: v for k, v in (data.tags or {}).items() if k.startswith("mlflow.")},
    }


def _run_metrics(client: MlflowClient, run_id: str) -> dict:
    r = client.get_run(run_id)
    metrics = dict(r.data.metrics or {})
    if not metrics:
        return {"run_id": run_id, "metrics": "(none logged)"}
    width = max(len(k) for k in metrics)
    lines = [f"run_id: {run_id}", f"status: {r.info.status}", ""]
    for k in sorted(metrics):
        lines.append(f"  {k.ljust(width)}  {metrics[k]}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _experiment_full(client: MlflowClient, exp_id: str) -> dict:
    e = client.get_experiment(exp_id)
    recent = client.search_runs(
        experiment_ids=[exp_id],
        max_results=5,
        order_by=["attributes.start_time DESC"],
    )
    return {
        "experiment_id": e.experiment_id,
        "name": e.name,
        "lifecycle_stage": e.lifecycle_stage,
        "artifact_location": e.artifact_location,
        "creation_time": _ms_to_iso(e.creation_time),
        "last_update_time": _ms_to_iso(e.last_update_time),
        "tags": dict(e.tags or {}),
        "recent_runs": [
            {
                "run_id": r.info.run_id,
                "run_name": r.info.run_name,
                "status": r.info.status,
                "start_time": _ms_to_iso(r.info.start_time),
            }
            for r in recent
        ],
    }


def _experiment_metrics(client: MlflowClient, exp_id: str) -> str:
    e = client.get_experiment(exp_id)
    runs = client.search_runs(
        experiment_ids=[exp_id],
        max_results=20,
        order_by=["attributes.start_time DESC"],
    )
    if not runs:
        return f"experiment: {e.name}\n(no runs)"
    # Aggregate latest metrics per metric key from the most recent run that has it.
    seen: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}
    for r in runs:
        for k, v in (r.data.metrics or {}).items():
            if k not in seen:
                seen[k] = (r.info.run_id, v)
    if not seen:
        return f"experiment: {e.name}\n(no metrics logged across recent runs)"
    width = max(len(k) for k in seen)
    lines = [f"experiment: {e.name}", f"runs scanned: {len(runs)}", ""]
    for k in sorted(seen):
        rid, v = seen[k]
        lines.append(f"  {k.ljust(width)}  {v}   ({rid[:8]})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _model_full(client: MlflowClient, name: str) -> dict:
    m = client.get_registered_model(name)
    return {
        "name": m.name,
        "description": m.description,
        "creation_timestamp": _ms_to_iso(m.creation_timestamp),
        "last_updated_timestamp": _ms_to_iso(m.last_updated_timestamp),
        "tags": dict(m.tags or {}),
        "latest_versions": [
            {
                "version": v.version,
                "stage": v.current_stage,
                "status": v.status,
                "run_id": v.run_id,
                "source": v.source,
                "creation_timestamp": _ms_to_iso(v.creation_timestamp),
            }
            for v in (m.latest_versions or [])
        ],
    }


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("kind", choices=["auto", "run", "experiment", "model"])
    ap.add_argument("id")
    ap.add_argument("--view", choices=["full", "metrics"], default="full")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    ident = args.id.strip()
    if not ident or ident == "0":
        uri = mlflow.get_tracking_uri() or "(unset)"
        print(
            "Help\n----\n"
            f"  current MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: {uri}\n\n"
            "  Set the env var and reload (Ctrl+R):\n"
            "    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow\n"
            "    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow\n"
            "    MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=file:./mlruns tv mlflow\n\n"
            "  Source cycle (Ctrl+S):  experiments -> runs-recent -> "
            "runs-experiment -> models\n"
            "  Preview cycle (Ctrl+F): full JSON   <->  metrics summary\n"
        )
        return 0

    kind = args.kind if args.kind != "auto" else _detect_kind(ident)
    client = MlflowClient()

    try:
        if kind == "run":
            payload = _run_full(client, ident) if args.view == "full" else _run_metrics(client, ident)
        elif kind == "experiment":
            payload = (
                _experiment_full(client, ident)
                if args.view == "full"
                else _experiment_metrics(client, ident)
            )
        elif kind == "model":
            # Models don't have a meaningful "metrics" view — fall back to full.
            payload = _model_full(client, ident)
        else:
            payload = f"# unknown kind: {kind}"
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        uri = mlflow.get_tracking_uri() or "(unset)"
        print(
            f"# preview failed for {kind} id={ident}\n"
            f"# tracking_uri: {uri}\n"
            f"# {type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
        )
        return 0

    _emit(payload)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```toml
# MLflow channel for television (tv).
# Browse experiments, runs, and registered models against any MLflow tracking
# backend (file:./mlruns, sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, or http://server:port).
#
# Usage:
#   tv mlflow
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - `mlflow` installed (provided by dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools — the
#     CLI binary is what we exec under the `uv run --script` shebang of the
#     two helpers).
#   - `uv` on PATH (installed by uv role; required to resolve the PEP 723
#     inline-deps block in mlflow-source.py / mlflow-preview.py).
#
# Backend mode is resolved entirely from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI. When unset,
# mlflow falls back to `file:./mlruns` in $PWD — this is mlflow's own default,
# not anything we add. To pin a backend at launch time:
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow
#
# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
#   1. Experiments     all active experiments
#   2. Recent runs     top 50 runs across all experiments, by start_time desc
#   3. Runs (scoped)   runs in $MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID (hint row when unset;
#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)
#   4. Models          registered models from the model registry
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. Full JSON       params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, timestamps
#   2. Metrics-only    sorted key=value table; or aggregated across recent
#                      runs for an experiment row
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Open full JSON detail in pager
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard
#   Ctrl+O     Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only; prints a hint
#              otherwise)
#   Alt+R      Re-launch tv scoped to the highlighted experiment row
#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal (paged)
#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
#
# No `watch` field: mlflow imports are heavy (~1s warm, several seconds cold);
# experiments and runs change on the minute scale anyway. Press Ctrl+R to
# refresh manually after logging a new run.
#
# Hint row sentinel: when the backend is unreachable or a source is unscoped,
# the helper emits a single row with id `__hint__`. Real mlflow ids never
# collide (experiment_ids are non-negative ints; run_ids are 32-hex; model
# names cannot contain `__hint__` in practice).

[metadata]
name = "mlflow"
description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]

[source]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
]
display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
no_sort = true

[preview]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"

[ui]
input_header = "MLflow"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open-detail"
# Override TV's default ctrl-y (which copies the entire display row) with
# id-only copy. Matches super-productivity.toml's convention.
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
alt-j = "actions:dump-json"

[actions.open-detail]
description = "Open full JSON detail in pager"
command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-id]
description = "Copy row id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.open-browser]
description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
# Build the URL inside the action so we read the live env var rather than
# baking it in. Inference mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
#   32-hex id -> need a roundtrip to find experiment_id, just open root
#   all-digit -> /#/experiments/<id>
#   else      -> /#/models/<name>
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://… — current: %s\\n' "${uri:-(unset)}"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener (open/xdg-open/wslview) — URL was: %s\\n' "$url"; sleep 2; fi"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.drill-runs]
description = "Re-launch tv scoped to the highlighted experiment (Alt+R)"
# Only meaningful on experiment rows (digit-only id). For run/model rows we
# print a friendly message and bail out so the user doesn't end up in an
# unscoped TV by accident.
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; case "$id" in __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row (id=%s). Move to the Experiments source (Ctrl+S) and try again.\\n' "$id"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.dump-json]
description = "Print full JSON detail to terminal, paged"
command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 02:26:11Z)**_

Channel is done and verified end-to-end. Summary:

**Files created** (untracked, ready to commit):
- `dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml` — channel: 4 source modes (experiments / runs-recent / runs-experiment / models), 2 preview modes (full JSON / metrics summary), 5 keybindings.
- `dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-source.py` — PEP 723 `uv run --script` helper, TSV emitter.
- `dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-preview.py` — PEP 723 helper, auto-detects entity kind from id shape.

**Why Python over CLI/REST**:
- `mlflow runs list` / `experiments search` emit Rich-formatted tables with no JSON flag — fragile to parse.
- REST API works only for `http(s)://` URIs; can't read `file:./mlruns` or `sqlite:///…`.
- `mlflow.MlflowClient` is the only path that handles all three backends uniformly.

**Verified backends**:
- LAN server `http://192.168.222.207:15002` — real experiments / runs / preview JSON ✓
- Local `file:./mlruns` in `/tmp/mlrun-test` — bootstrap + smoke run listed ✓
- `sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow-sqlite-test.db` — bootstrap + preview JSON ✓
- Unreachable host `http://no-such-host:9999` — fails fast in 4s (was 60s+ without `MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=5`), emits clean hint row ✓
- `tv list-channels` includes `mlflow` (TV parses the TOML at startup) ✓

**Notable gotchas resolved during implementation**:
1. **`0` cannot be the hint sentinel** — MLflow's default backend assigns `experiment_id=0` to the auto-created "Default" experiment. Switched sentinel to `__hint__`.
2. **`logging.setLevel` must run after `import mlflow`** — mlflow installs its handlers at import time; pre-import setLevel calls get overwritten and `mlflow.store.db.utils: Creating initial MLflow database tables...` was leaking to stderr (which TV does not suppress).
3. **MLflow HTTP defaults are too patient** — 120s timeout × 5 retries means TV hangs ~60s on a typo'd URI before the hint row appears. Pinned `MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=5` + `MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES=1`.
4. **mlflow 3.12 auto-detects backend from CWD** — uv resolves `mlflow>=3.4` to 3.12.0, which sees `mlflow.db` in CWD and uses sqlite automatically. Updated channel doc comment to reflect this.

**Usage**:
```
tv mlflow                                            # uses CWD auto-detect
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
```
Inside TV: `Ctrl+S` cycles source · `Ctrl+F` cycles preview · `Enter` opens JSON in pager · `Ctrl+Y` copies id · `Ctrl+O` opens in browser (HTTP only) · `Alt+R` re-launches scoped to highlighted experiment · `Alt+J` dumps JSON.

First `tv mlflow` invocation will take ~2min while `uv` builds the inline-deps venv (mlflow + transitive ~80MB); subsequent runs are ~1s warm.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 02:39:42Z)**_

Done. Commit `81358eb` on `main`.

### What landed

**1. Colorful preview** — all four view modes (run-full / run-metrics / experiment-full / experiment-metrics / hint) now emit valid JSON, piped through `bat -l json --color=always --plain --paging=never` from the channel TOML. Truecolor ANSI verified via `od -c`. Rich-via-Console was dropped; bat through a pipe is what super-productivity does (`jq -C`) for the same reason — TV preserves ANSI on preview output.

**2. Nested drill-down** — Enter is now kind-aware via `[actions.open-or-drill]`:
- Experiment row (digit-only id) → `MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID=<id> tv mlflow --source-command="…runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / <name>"`. A fresh nested TV scoped to that experiment's runs only, with the breadcrumb in the header.
- Run / model / hint row → open JSON detail in `less -R` (previous behavior).
- `Alt+R` remains as an explicit-drill alias for muscle memory.

The drill is a single-level stack: Esc exits the nested TV back to the shell (not to the outer experiments list), because TV doesn't have a built-in back-stack. The user just re-runs `tv mlflow` for cross-experiment views — same UX as `tv channels`.

**3. Gitleaks false-positive** — MLflow's REST API returns base64-encoded pagination cursors in `next_page_token` (e.g. `eyJvZmZzZXQiOiAyfQ==` = `{"offset":2}`). Gitleaks's `generic-api-key` entropy heuristic flagged these in the transcript. Added two allowlist entries to `.gitleaks.toml`:
- Global: JSON-shape `"next_page_token": "…"` / `"nextPageToken": "…"` (covers committed code/docs that legitimately show API responses).
- Path-scoped to agent transcripts: bare `next_page_token` token name in any form (covers markdown backticks, narration, etc.).

Both are safe — these tokens are session-scoped pagination state, not credentials, and several major APIs use this exact field name (Google APIs, MLflow, others).

### Try it
```
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
```
- `Ctrl+F` toggles preview between full JSON and metrics summary (both colorized).
- On any experiment row, press **Enter** → drill into just that experiment's runs.
- `Esc` exits back to the shell.
